papers.abstract: To characterize EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression in human brain tumors and evaluate the preclinical antitumor activity of EPHRIN-B2-based chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in 141 specimens from 116 patients; 113 specimens were included in analyses by histological category. EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells were generated using the piggyBac transposon system. In vitro activity was evaluated against six brain tumor cell lines and a receptor-negative control line. Intracerebroventricular administration was assessed in two intracranial xenograft models, with mock T cells, control CAR-T cells, and phosphate-buffered saline as comparators. EPHA2 expression was observed across histological categories, whereas higher EPHB4 expression was predominantly found in high-grade tumors. Among glioblastoma/gliosarcoma specimens, 74% and 37% had staining scores ≥ 2 for EPHA2 and EPHB4, respectively. High expression of both receptors within the same specimen was concentrated in high-grade tumors. CAR-T cells reduced viable tumor cell numbers and increased interferon-γ and interleukin-2 secretion against all six brain tumor cell lines, whereas no significant differences were detected with the receptor-negative control. Although differences from control T cells did not reach statistical significance, EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells reduced tumor signals relative to saline-treated controls at selected time points in both xenograft models. These findings characterize EPHA2 and EPHB4 expression in human brain tumors and demonstrate in vitro antitumor activity of EPHRIN-B2-based CAR-T cells, providing a basis for further studies to establish CAR-specific efficacy in intracranial tumors. papers.abstract: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBL) is a rare and biologically distinct subtype of aggressive B-cell lymphoma that predominantly affects young adults. Despite substantial therapeutic advances, several aspects of its management remain controversial, including frontline treatment selection, the role of radiotherapy, PET-based response assessment, and the optimal sequencing of immunotherapies in relapsed disease. Drawing on prospective and retrospective studies, cooperative group data, expert consensus and our own real-world experience, we present a practical case-based approach across the disease course, built around four clinical cases followed to their resolution and covering diagnosis, frontline treatment, PET-guided response assessment, pregnancy-associated disease, adolescents and young adults, relapsed or refractory disease, and long-term follow-up. We focus on decision-making where evidence remains limited, including the integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), CAR-T cell therapy, radiotherapy and transplantation, and the emerging role of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and radiomics. Management increasingly relies on individualized, multidisciplinary decision-making that integrates disease biology, functional imaging and patient characteristics to maximize cure while minimizing long-term toxicity. In our practice this translates into dose-intensified frontline chemoimmunotherapy rather than R-CHOP21, omission of radiotherapy after a complete metabolic response and, where these treatments are accessible, a second-line strategy built on checkpoint inhibitors and anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, with early referral for cellular therapy in refractory or early relapse.

papers.abstract: Vestibular schwannoma (VS) is a common benign intracranial tumor for which Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) is an important treatment option. However, post-treatment changes in tumor volume vary considerably and can complicate follow-up and response assessment. This study developed a framework that uses deep learning-based segmentation and MRI radiomics to predict long-term treatment response to GKRS for VS. We developed an nnU-Net model to automate VS segmentation on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI. Patients with long-term follow-up after GKRS were classified into four response patterns: direct regression, delayed regression, stable disease, and growth. A two-stage machine-learning framework was then constructed. Stage 1 distinguishes regression from non-regression, while Stage 2 differentiates direct from delayed regression. Pretreatment MRI radiomics features were combined with clinical and dose-related variables and used to train multiple machine-learning models. The models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, and SHAP analysis was used to interpret the results. The nnU-Net model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 91.16 ± 0.47% on the external test dataset. Among the 155 patients, 53 showed direct regression, 83 delayed regression, 9 stable disease, and 10 tumor growths. In Stage 1, the Balanced Random Forest algorithm achieved accuracy of 74.19 ± 7.21%, an AUROC of 72.43 ± 10.18%, and AUPRC of 93.08 ± 4.27%. In Stage 2, the Support Vector Machine achieved accuracy of 64.05 ± 4.16%, an AUROC of 66.70 ± 6.21%, and AUPRC of 57.10 ± 7.30%. SHAP analysis identified radiomics and dose-related features as important predictors. Deep learning-based segmentation combined with pretreatment MRI radiomics, clinical variables, and dose-related parameters may provide useful information for predicting long-term response after GKRS for VS. This framework could support more individualized follow-up planning and help clinicians distinguish delayed regression from treatment failure.

papers.abstract: Tumor metabolic reprogramming is a dynamic and context-dependent process that supports malignant progression, adaptation to microenvironmental stress, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Understanding the interplay between tumor-intrinsic metabolic alterations and the tumor microenvironment (TME) is essential for identifying actionable metabolic vulnerabilities and developing more effective therapeutic strategies. This review examines the reprogramming of glucose, lipid, amino acid, and mitochondrial metabolism, together with the oncogenic, tumor-suppressive, epigenetic, and post-transcriptional mechanisms that regulate these processes. It highlights the bidirectional metabolic interactions between cancer cells, stromal cells, and immune populations, focusing on nutrient competition, metabolite exchange, hypoxia, and acidosis as drivers of immune suppression and tumor progression. The diagnostic and prognostic applications of metabolic imaging and metabolite-derived biomarkers are also discussed. Furthermore, current therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic enzymes, transporters, and tumor-specific metabolic dependencies are evaluated, with particular attention to combination approaches involving chemotherapy, molecularly targeted agents, and immunotherapy. Key translational challenges, including intratumoral metabolic heterogeneity, compensatory pathway adaptation, toxicity to normal tissues, and insufficient biomarker validation, are considered alongside emerging opportunities for precision metabolic therapy. Tumor metabolic reprogramming represents an interconnected and adaptive network rather than a collection of isolated pathway alterations. Therapeutic efficacy will depend on identifying context-specific metabolic dependencies while accounting for tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental influences, and adaptive resistance. Integrating metabolic profiling and validated biomarkers with rational combination therapies may facilitate patient stratification and support the development of more selective and durable anticancer treatments. Tumor metabolic reprogramming integrates glucose, lipid, amino acid, and mitochondrial metabolism to support malignant progression and stress adaptation. Bidirectional metabolic crosstalk between tumor, stromal, and immune cells reshapes the tumor microenvironment, promoting immune evasion and therapeutic resistance. Integrating metabolic imaging, biomarker profiling, and context-specific metabolic targeting may enable rational combination therapies and more precise cancer treatment.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the scientific literature on active surveillance (AS) for small renal masses (SRMs) using bibliometric methods and to characterize publication trends, leading contributors, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution. The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 28 July 2026 for English-language articles and reviews published from 2006 onward. After title/abstract and full-text screening, eligible records were analyzed using the bibliometrix package (biblioshiny) in R and VOSviewer. Publication and citation trends; the productivity of countries, institutions, journals, and authors; co-authorship and co-citation networks; keyword co-occurrence; trend topics; and a thematic map were evaluated. The study included 480 publications (356 articles and 124 reviews) published between 2007 and 2026 in 153 journals. These publications received 14,369 citations (mean, 29.95 per publication; h-index, 57). Annual output increased at an annual growth rate of 4.48% and peaked in 2022 (n = 45). Co-authorship analysis identified nine clusters, led by the prospective phase 2 study of the Toronto-led Renal Cell Carcinoma of Canada group, the DISSRM Registry Consortium, and the Fox Chase Cancer Center group. Keyword trends shifted from natural history and disease progression toward imaging, oncocytoma, population-based data, and contrast-enhanced ultrasound. No motor themes were identified on the thematic map. Research on AS for SRMs has grown more slowly than other areas of kidney cancer research and remains concentrated in a few North American centers and their prospective registries. The central question has shifted from whether a mass will grow to which masses should be observed.

papers.abstract: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma (GCA) of the appendix is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited data on the role of adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) in stage III disease. This study evaluated the association between AC and survival in the largest stage III GCA cohort to date. The National Cancer Database was queried for patients with stage III GCA (2010-2021). Overall survival (OS) was assessed from a 60-day postoperative landmark to address immortal time bias using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression with covariates selected by a directed acyclic graph. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Of 418 patients, 273 (65.3 %) received AC. The 5-year OS with versus without AC was 75.5 % versus 69.5 % in stage IIIA/B (p = 0.27), and was 29.9 % versus 12.3 % in stage IIIC disease (p = 0.07). In the landmark multivariable model, AC was not associated with OS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.85; 95 % confidence interval [CI], 0.54-1.34), including its use in stage IIIA/B (aHR, 0.90; 95 % CI, 0.53-1.50) and stage IIIC (aHR, 0.55; 95 % CI, 0.25-1.24) disease. Worse OS was associated with stage IIIC disease (aHR, 4.23), age ≥75 years (aHR, 6.20), Charlson-Deyo score ≥2 (aHR, 2.01), and residual tumor at the margin (aHR, 2.71). Results were similar with IPTW (aHR, 0.83; 95 % CI, 0.65-1.05). Adjuvant chemotherapy was not significantly associated with OS after multivariable adjustment or IPTW. However, wide confidence intervals, particularly in stage IIIC disease, preclude exclusion of a clinically meaningful benefit, supporting further investigation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with venous tumor thrombus (VTT) remains a surgically complex entity traditionally stratified by the Mayo thrombus classification. The prognostic roles of tumor biological features and perioperative systemic therapy in contemporary multidisciplinary practice remain to be clarified. This study evaluated oncologic outcomes, identified independent prognostic factors, and reassessed the prognostic relevance of thrombus extent versus tumor biology in RCC with VTT. This retrospective single-center study included 467 consecutive patients undergoing radical nephrectomy with tumor thrombectomy between 2014 and 2024. Cancer-specific survival (CSS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimation and multivariable Cox regression. The Peking University Third Hospital (PKUTH) risk model was developed and internally validated for risk stratification, and the association of postoperative systemic therapy with CSS was explored across risk groups. After a median follow-up of 27.7 months (maximum 121.6 months), the 5 year CSS rate for the entire cohort was 59.3%. On multivariable analysis, five independent predictors of CSS were identified: distant metastasis (hazard ratio [HR] 2.69), non-clear cell histology (HR 2.29), perinephric fat invasion (HR 1.54), tumor necrosis (HR 1.51), and higher preoperative hemoglobin (protective factor, HR 0.48). The PKUTH risk model showed modest-to-good discrimination with a concordance index of 0.739. Postoperative systemic therapy was associated with a potential survival advantage in high-risk patients. Long-term survival in RCC with VTT is driven primarily by tumor biology rather than thrombus level. The PKUTH risk model enables clinically meaningful risk stratification and may help identify patients who could potentially benefit from intensified postoperative systemic therapy.

papers.abstract: Although sentinel lymph node mapping has become the standard approach for surgical staging in early-stage endometrial cancer, systematic pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) continues to play an important role in selected patients with intermediate- and high-risk disease.1 Furthermore, PLND is a fundamental surgical procedure, performed not only for gynecologic oncology procedures, but also for colorectal and urologic oncology procedures.2,3 This video demonstrates the key anatomical landmarks and our standardized anatomy-based concept for en bloc PLND, followed by its implementation using the da Vinci SP surgical system (SP), a newer single-port robotic platform. A 66-year-old woman with preoperatively diagnosed early-stage uterine serous carcinoma (p53-positive) underwent single-port robotic staging surgery, including simple hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection, and partial omentectomy. The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. A standardized, anatomy-based approach using reproducible anatomical landmarks facilitated safe and systematic en bloc PLND. Suspension of the vesicohypogastric fascia (umbilical artery) provided stable exposure of the retroperitoneal space, while the articulating snake-like instruments of the SP platform enabled precise traction and countertraction, facilitating meticulous dissection throughout the procedure. Final histopathological examination confirmed stage IIC uterine serous carcinoma. The patient subsequently received adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy and remains disease-free at the latest follow-up. The SP platform enables standardized, anatomy-based, en bloc PLND while adhering to fundamental oncologic principles. The anatomical concepts and technical strategies may facilitate reproducible surgical practice and may be applicable across multiple specialties in pelvic oncology.

papers.abstract: Hepatic progression is common in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We evaluated hepatic arterial infusion (HAI) floxuridine (FUDR) added to systemic chemotherapy in selected patients with synchronous liver-dominant metastatic PDAC. PANCPUMP was a prospective, single-center, single-arm phase II pilot study of 14 patients with synchronous PDAC liver metastases and stable disease or response after at least 2 months of systemic chemotherapy. Patients underwent HAI pump placement and received up to six 28 day cycles of HAI FUDR with systemic therapy. The primary endpoint was 1 year hepatic progression-free survival, with a prespecified target of 40%. Seven patients (50%) remained free of hepatic progression at 1 year, meeting the primary endpoint. Median time to hepatic progression was 15.7 months when deaths without hepatic progression were censored; median all-site progression-free interval and overall survival were 14.5 and 14.0 months, respectively. Five patients (35.7%) survived at least 24 months. Biochemical hepatotoxicity was frequent; two delayed grade 3 gastroduodenal artery (GDA)/catheter-associated vascular complications occurred. Among 10 patients with paired European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Core Quality-of-Life questionnaire assessments, the mean global health/quality-of-life score was 69.2 at baseline and 70.0 at first follow-up (p = 0.91). HAI FUDR plus systemic therapy met the prespecified hepatic-control endpoint in a highly selected cohort. These proof-of-concept findings support further study of regional hepatic therapy alongside contemporary systemic treatment.

papers.abstract: Despite the standardization of Cytoreductive surgery (CRS), recurrence of disseminated appendiceal neoplasms remains a concern with rates as high as 70% reported. This study aimed to define the pattern and predictors of disease recurrence following index CRS from the experiences of a high-volume center. This was a cohort study that analyzed patients that underwent CRS for an appendiceal neoplasm between January 1996 and April 2025 in Sydney, Australia. Recurrence patterns were followed through and compared to patients' clinicopathological and perioperative characteristics around the time of index CRS. A total of 587 patients underwent a complete cytoreduction for an appendiceal neoplasm. The median follow up period was 46 months. The mean PCI at the time of index surgery was 23 + 12 and high grade neoplasms made up 48% of the cohort. Recurrence free survival at 1-, 5-, and 10-years was 85% versus 68%, 60% versus 29% and 51% versus 21% for low grade versus high-grade neoplasms respectively (p < 0.001). Signet ring cell presence (hazard ratio [HR] = 3.173), increasing PCI (HR= 1.029) and a Ca19.9 greater than 10x the upper limit of normal during index CRS (HR = 2.571) were predictive of disease recurrence; while the use of early postoperative intraperitoneal chemotherapy (EPIC) was protective (HR = 0.569). A raised Ca19.9 at the time of index CRS-HIPEC independently correlated with the volume of small bowel disease during repeat CRS. Several factors influence the risk of recurrence following CRS-HIPEC for appendiceal neoplasms. This information may be used to guide prognosis and surveillance protocols.

papers.abstract: Extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness elevation, a prominent mechanical attribute in liver cirrhosis, is a key driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) modification regulates multiple RNA species to influence tumorigenesis, but its role in mechanotransduction-especially in response to matrix stiffness-remains unclear. Here, we found that increased matrix stiffness enhances HCC cell proliferation and metastasis, accompanied by elevated global m5C levels. High stiffness triggers autocrine transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) secretion in HCC cells, which activates transcription factor Smad3 to upregulate NSUN2, a core m5C methyltransferase. Clinically, high NSUN2 expression and elevated m5C levels correlate with poor prognosis in HCC patients. Further studies showed NSUN2 directly binds to HSP90AA1 mRNA, enhances its m5C modification, and recruits the m5C reader ALYREF to stabilize HSP90AA1 mRNA. We also confirmed the matrix stiffness-NSUN2-HSP90AA1 axis activates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, forming a pro-tumor cascade that promotes HCC growth and progression. Notably, we identified Vilanterol as a candidate NSUN2-targeting compound that effectively downregulates NSUN2 expression and global m5C levels and suppresses HCC malignant phenotypes. Collectively, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized regulatory axis, the matrix stiffness-NSUN2-HSP90AA1-ER stress axis, in HCC, and suggest that Vilanterol may serve as a promising therapeutic agent for HCC.

papers.abstract: CD19 CAR-T therapy achieves high remission rates in relapsed/refractory (R/R) B-cell lymphoma but is often limited by PD1/PD-L1-mediated immune suppression. A PD1/CD28 switch receptor may convert inhibitory PD1 signals into CD28 costimulation, enhancing efficacy. In this single-center, phase I trial, adults with R/R B-cell lymphoma received autologous CD19 CAR-T cells incorporating a PD1/CD28 switch receptor. Treatment followed a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design with subsequent expansion cohorts. Primary endpoints were safety and feasibility; secondary endpoints included efficacy, survival, CAR-T kinetics, and biomarker correlations. Thirty-two patients received CAR-T cells. In dose escalation, 6/9 responded (overall response rate [ORR] 66.7%; complete response [CR] 44.4%). Based on favorable responses at the highest dose (3 × 10^6/kg), 23 additional patients were treated, yielding ORR 87.0% and CR 69.6%. At median follow-up of 34 months, median duration of response (DOR) and overall survival (OS) were not reached; 12- and 36-month DOR rates were 58.6% and 53.3%. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 12 months, with 3-year PFS 43.3%; 1- and 3-year OS were 82% and 64%. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 62.5% (all grade 1-2) and neurotoxicity in 6.3% (grade 2-3). No significant association was detected between baseline PD-L1 expression and response. CD19&PD1/CD28 CAR-T therapy achieved high response rates, durable remissions, and manageable toxicity in R/R B-cell lymphoma. Responses occurred across baseline PD-L1 strata, but the single-arm design precludes attribution of efficacy to the switch receptor. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT03932955.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) recurrence is associated with invasion and therapeutic resistance, but the contribution of neuron-derived signals remains incompletely defined. We combined analyses of primary and recurrent GBM transcriptomic datasets and paired patient tissues with functional studies in cultures derived from primary GBM. Neuronal fractions were higher in the sampled recurrent specimens, and CellChat inferred higher neuron-to-tumor NRG3-ERBB4 communication probabilities in recurrent samples. In five matched tissue pairs, recurrent specimens had a higher percentage of TUBB3-positive cells and higher NRG3 H-scores than their primary counterparts. Recombinant NRG3 increased migration and BrdU incorporation in a subset of patient-derived cultures (PDCs). CYT-1 depletion and complementary CYT-1/CYT-2 expression experiments supported a contribution of ERBB4 isoform composition to these responses. NRG3 induced PI3K-AKT signaling and increased RUNX2 abundance relative to each culture's baseline. Genetic RUNX2 depletion and AKT inhibition reduced NRG3-associated BrdU incorporation, supporting an AKT-RUNX2 contribution to the proliferative phenotype. Spatial analyses associated RUNX2 with mesenchymal and extracellular matrix programs near neuron-containing regions. Neuronal Nrg3 depletion reduced intracranial tumor burden and interface-associated RUNX2 staining in xenograft models. Afatinib and CADD522 each reduced intracranial tumor burden in xenografts derived from primary GBM cultures. Together, these findings support a role for neuronal NRG3-ERBB4 signaling in GBM cell invasion and implicate AKT-dependent RUNX2 induction in the proliferative response of NRG3-responsive cultures.

papers.abstract: Dysregulated KRAS activity is a major driver of colorectal cancer progression, yet the role of phosphatases in regulating KRAS phosphorylation and activity remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify dual-specificity phosphatase 4 (DUSP4) as a KRAS phosphatase that binds to and dephosphorylates both wild-type and mutant KRAS. Elevated DUSP4 expression increased GTP-bound KRAS levels and promoted colorectal cancer cell proliferation and tumor growth. Conversely, genetic depletion of Dusp4 reduced tumor burden in ApcMin/+-driven colorectal cancer models. Mechanistically, DUSP4 dephosphorylated KRAS at threonine 2 and tyrosine 4, thereby limiting GTPase-activating protein-mediated GTP hydrolysis and maintaining KRAS in its active, GTP-bound state. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of DUSP4 with tanshinone IIA suppressed colorectal cancer growth and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of cetuximab in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer. Collectively, our findings establish a role for DUSP4-mediated dephosphorylation in regulating KRAS activity and suggest that targeting DUSP4 may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for colorectal cancer.

papers.abstract: Long-term aspirin use has been associated with a reduced risk of colorectal cancer (CRC), but its impact on metastatic disease at diagnosis is less studied. This study investigated the associations between low-dose aspirin use and the presence of distant metastases at CRC diagnosis. Using the Colorectal Cancer Database Sweden (CRCBaSe), exposure to low-dose aspirin was defined as ≥12 months of use and categorized as non-users, past users, or current users. Adjusted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 81,269 CRC patients, 18,943 (23%) had synchronous distant metastases; 15,424 (19%) were current and 5,044 (6%) past aspirin users. Current users had lower odds of synchronous metastases, (ORadj 0.86, 95% CI 0.82-0.90), most pronounced in right-sided colon cancer (ORadj 0.79, 95% CI 0.74-0.86). In duration-dependent analyses, the reduction persisted in right-sided colon cancer regardless of use duration, and among rectal cancer patients with specific use patterns, but not in left-sided colon cancer. Past users had reduced odds of synchronous metastases only in right-sided colon cancer (ORadj 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.92), independent of use duration. Low-dose aspirin use was associated with lower odds of distant metastases at CRC diagnosis, particularly in right-sided colon cancer.

papers.abstract: Few studies with pre-diagnostic samples have estimated associations between circulating metabolites and risk of advanced prostate cancer. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of pre-diagnostic blood samples from 212 advanced prostate cancer cases (stage ≥ T3b or lethal during follow-up) and 212 matched controls from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study. 243 metabolites were assayed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (Broad Institute) and met quality control standards. We used multivariable conditional logistic regression to generate odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) for associations between individual metabolites and risk of advanced prostate cancer, and conducted metabolite set enrichment tests to identify metabolite classes enriched in advanced prostate cancer. Subgroup analyses were conducted by body mass index (BMI) and time between blood draw and diagnosis. Levels of 16 lipid metabolites were nominally associated with advanced prostate cancer at p < 0.05, though none were statistically significant after multiple testing correction. The strongest signals were for C56:1 triacylglycerol (TAG; OR: 1.34, 95% CI: 1.07-1.67) and C38:4 diacylglycerol (DAG; OR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.04-1.55). Enrichment analyses revealed six metabolite classes associated with advanced prostate cancer after multiple testing adjustment, the top four of which were DAGs and TAGs: DAGs overall (p = 3.4E-07), unsaturated DAGs (p = 5.9E-07), unsaturated TAGs (p = 2.3E-06), and TAGs overall (p = 2.4E-06). 48 metabolites were nominally associated with advanced prostate cancer among individuals with BMI < 25 kg/m2; only three demonstrated nominal associations in individuals with BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2. These findings suggest a possible relationship between circulating pre-diagnostic lipid levels and aggressive prostate cancer risk, particularly in lean individuals.

papers.abstract: Expert contour quality assurance (QA) in multi-center radiation therapy trials is labor-intensive and scales poorly. We evaluated whether an FDA-cleared AI auto-segmentation tool can serve as a high-sensitivity screening aid for contour QA in the genitourinary (GU) trial NRG-GU010. Data from 579 patients submitted to NRG-GU010 (NCT05050084) were studied in two cohorts: the first 52 consecutive submissions (one excluded for an unavailable planning CT; 51 analyzed) for a consensus-based agreement analysis, and the subsequent 527 for large-cohort workflow validation. AI-generated contours were compared with submitted contours using four geometric indices (Dice similarity, Hausdorff distance, mean distance to agreement, percent volume change) against thresholds from prior per-protocol cases, producing target-volume (TV) and organ-at-risk (OAR) scores of 1 (per-protocol), 2 (acceptable variation), or 3 (unacceptable deviation). The 51-case cohort used multi-expert adjudicated consensus as reference; the 527-case cohort used each case's single reviewing principal investigator (PI) under a triage framework (AI-positive = score 2 or 3; PI-positive = score 3). Agreement was assessed with quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa; sensitivity and specificity are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). In the consensus cohort, AI identified all four unacceptable (score-3) OAR deviations (sensitivity 1.00; 95% CI, 0.40-1.00); no consensus score-3 TV cases were present. Quadratic-weighted kappa was 0.71 (0.40-0.90) for OAR and 0.53 (0.31-0.74) for TV. In the 527-case validation cohort, AI triage sensitivity was 100% for both TV (5/5) and OAR (4/4) score-3 deviations, with case-level specificity of 69% (TV) and 25% (OAR) and 100% negative predictive value for both. AI-assisted contour comparison served as a high-sensitivity triage tool, flagging all clinically unacceptable deviations while clearing AI-negative cases, supporting its use as a screening aid-not a replacement-for expert contour QA in GU clinical trials. Lower specificity (particularly for OARs) and few score-3 events warrant further disease-site-specific validation.

papers.abstract: Radiation-induced xerostomia is a clinically significant adverse effect of head and neck radiotherapy with limited treatment options. This prospective, single-arm case series evaluated the safety, feasibility, and exploratory clinical efficacy of ultrasound-guided intraglandular administration of allogeneic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (UC-MSCs) in patients with chronic radiation-induced xerostomia. Ten disease-free survivors of oropharyngeal cancer with CTCAE grade 2-3 xerostomia received ultrasound-guided UC-MSC injections into both parotid and submandibular glands. Each parotid gland received 50 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs and each submandibular gland 25 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs. Safety was the primary outcome. Exploratory assessments were performed at baseline and at 1 and 4 months and included patient-reported outcome measures, unstimulated and stimulated salivary flow rates, salivary biochemical analyses, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound shear-wave elastography, salivary gland scintigraphy, and, where feasible, core-needle biopsy. No serious adverse events were observed. Procedure-related effects were limited to transient injection-site pain, swelling, and local discomfort. Objective salivary flow rates and most biochemical parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. In contrast, patient-reported outcomes improved, with the greatest changes at 4 months. Xerostomia Questionnaire scores decreased from 63.44 ± 16.81 at baseline to 53.18 ± 21.16 at 4 months (p = 0.0066), and visual analogue scale scores from 64.65 ± 17.30 to 60.29 ± 18.11 (p = 0.0122). Improvements were also observed in xerostomia and sticky saliva domains of the EORTC QLQ-H&N35. MRI showed only subtle changes in T2-weighted signal intensity ratios, while elastography remained unchanged. Scintigraphy demonstrated increased excretion velocity at 4 months (p = 0.0355). In this single-arm case series of 10 patients, ultrasound-guided intraglandular UC-MSC administration was feasible and well tolerated over four months, with no serious adverse events. Improvements in PROMs and scintigraphic excretion velocity were exploratory findings in the absence of a control group and occurred despite largely unchanged salivary flow. Clinical efficacy remains to be established in adequately powered, randomized, placebo-controlled trials.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy is now standard for multiple solid tumors; however, substantial heterogeneity in treatment response remains. Current biomarkers such as programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) capture only limited molecular dimensions of tumor biology. We aimed to predict pathological response from pretreatment hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs), benchmark it against PD-L1, and test cross-cancer transferability. Across 320 patients, 377 pretreatment H&E WSIs were processed, yielding 20,247,535 tissue patches. We developed PIRPath (Pathomics for Immunotherapy Response Prediction), a region-guided weakly supervised framework, internally validated in a breast cancer cohort using five-fold cross-validation and further evaluated in two independent external cohorts. Exploratory cross-cancer transfer was assessed in lung cancer and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cohorts. In breast cancer, PIRPath-BC achieved an AUC of 0.9318 (95% CI, 0.8836-0.9713) in internal validation and external AUCs of 0.7991 (95% CI, 0.6000-0.9509) and 0.7292 (95% CI, 0.5333-0.8947). High-score patients showed significantly higher pathological complete response (pCR) rates than low-score patients in both cohorts (78.6%vs 31.2%, P = 0.010; 70.6% vs 35.3%, P = 0.039). In cross-cancer transfer, PIRPath reached 0.7107 for major pathological response (MPR) and 0.7037 for pCR, versus 0.6125 and 0.4590 for PD-L1. Incremental analyses demonstrated additional predictive value beyond PD-L1. Exploratory transcriptomic analyses linked predictions to reduced stromal features and immune activation-related states. H&E WSIs contain response-associated histological information not fully captured by conventional biomarkers. PIRPath provides a computational pathology framework for extracting this and complementing existing biomarkers in neoadjuvant immunotherapy stratification, although the modest external cohorts require prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Progressive stiffening of the extracellular matrix (ECM), driven by excessive collagen deposition and crosslinking, is a hallmark of breast cancer progression. While ECM mechanics profoundly influence tumor behavior and fate, the mechanisms by which matrix stiffening regulates exosome biogenesis and release remain poorly understood. To investigate the impact of matrix stiffness on exosome secretion, polyacrylamide gels with defined stiffness were employed. Cancer cells-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEV) were characterized and quantified using nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), bead-based assays, and reporter cell systems. Mechanistic insights were obtained through immunofluorescence (IF), proximity ligation assay (PLA), TEM, immunoblotting, and immunoprecipitation. A stiffness-tunable NOD-SCID xenograft model was used to validate the effect of stiffness on exosome secretion in vivo. Additionally, human breast cancer tissue microarrays were analyzed to examine the associations among collagen remodeling, exosome secretion pathways, and clinical outcomes. We unravel a dual mechanism by which stiff ECM enhances exosome output. Increased matrix rigidity promotes intraluminal vesicle formation by enhancing HSP90-TSG101 association, thereby stimulating ESCRT-dependent exosome biogenesis, while simultaneously facilitating multivesicular body docking for fusion with the plasma membrane via upregulation of Rab27a. Rab27a expression is controlled by KIBRA, a regulator of YAP/TAZ mechanosignaling. Genetic depletion of KIBRA or Rab27a markedly suppresses stiffness-induced exosome secretion and abolishes ECM-driven motility and invasion in vitro. In stiffness-tunable xenograft models, stiff ECM accelerates tumor growth and elevates circulating sEV levels, effects reversed by Rab27a silencing. Furthermore, analysis of human breast tumor tissues revealed that a highly bundled and crosslinked collagen architecture - indicative of higher stiffness - correlated with increased colocalization of Rab27a and KIBRA, coupled with an unfavorable clinical prognosis. Collectively, our findings uncover a novel mechanoresponsive reliance of HSP90-TSG101 and KIBRA-Rab27a axes that link ECM stiffness to exosomes-driven tumor aggressiveness, highlighting new avenues for mechano-targeting of breast malignancies.

papers.abstract: An increasing proportion of complex surgical procedures are being performed in the UK as day-cases, and NHS targets aim for these to encompass ≥ 75% of all surgeries. There has been limited outcome follow-up for this group of patients, particularly considering the prevalence of persistent postoperative opioid use and factors associated with its occurrence. Data from POPPY, a national, prospective, observational study exploring outcomes following day-case surgery in the UK, were used to estimate the prevalence of persistent postoperative opioid use at day 97 following surgery. Patient, anaesthetic and surgical factors associated with increased persistent postoperative opioid use were explored using multivariable analysis. Of the 7839 initially recruited patients, 3488 (44.5%) provided details of their analgesic medication at day 97 following surgery. The prevalence of daily persistent postoperative opioid use was estimated to be 11.8% (95%CI 11.1-13.2%). Patient factors associated with daily persistent postoperative opioid use were pre-operative opioid use; opioid use at day 7; and composite pain scores (day 1, day 3 and day 7). Compared with general surgery, ENT, breast and orthopaedic surgery carried a higher risk of persistent postoperative opioid use. Patient factors associated with a reduced odds ratio of persistent postoperative opioid use were: female sex; higher composite pain score at baseline; and Index of Multiple Deprivation quintile 4. Daily persistent postoperative opioid use at day 97 following surgery was associated with reduced quality of life scores. Daily persistent postoperative opioid use is common in the UK following day-case surgery. Patient and surgical factors that are associated with an increased risk of this outcome could be used to drive improvement in identification of at-risk patients pre-operatively and optimise postoperative prescribing pathways.

papers.abstract: Principles of effective antimicrobial stewardship include prescription of empiric therapy based on the most likely causative organism, with medication review within 72 h. Adherence to best practice in UK ICUs is unknown and the aim of this study was to evaluate patient- and unit-level antimicrobial use in UK ICUs. We conducted a prospective national audit of antimicrobial use in adults (aged ≥ 18 y) admitted to ICUs in the UK and Isle of Man with a point-prevalence survey. Subsequently, we collected longitudinal data on review of therapy and antimicrobial resistance in a subset of patients who had commenced therapy within the previous 3 days. We studied 2626 patients from 154/292 (52.7%) ICUs. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 1592 (60.6%) patients. Of 2116 empiric antimicrobial orders, 1592 (75.2%) were compliant with unit-level guidelines. For non-compliant orders, 253 (12.0% of all empiric orders) were discussed with infection specialists and 69 (3.3%) provided justification for off-guidance therapy, but 202 (9.5%) were prescribed outside guidance without justification or discussion with infection specialists. Guideline-compliant review within 72 h of prescription took place in 1488/1606 (92.7%) eligible medication orders. A pre-specified stop or review date was strongly associated with antimicrobial review within 72 h (adjusted OR 9.3, 95%CI 5.4-16.2). We have benchmarked critical care antimicrobial stewardship and guideline compliance across the UK. We recommend that pre-specified review dates are added to all prescriptions, as the most important determinant of review identified in our audit. Future work should include national stewardship audit cycles to benchmark practice and inform quality improvement initiatives.

papers.abstract: Day-29 minimal residual disease (MRD) is central to risk assessment in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but MRD alone may not fully explain outcome heterogeneity. We performed a retrospective patient-level analysis of the public TARGET/cBioPortal cohort to evaluate whether MRD and candidate adverse molecular alterations (CAMA) jointly stratify event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS). The roster contained 1551 patients; MRD was available for 1534, including 1058 below 0.01% and 476 at or above 0.01%. EFS and OS source fields were available for 1535, with 399 coded EFS events and 254 deaths. Their intersection with available MRD contained 1524 patients, 391 EFS events and 246 deaths. Molecular profiles were selectively available: 137 patients had mutation profiles and 682 had copy-number profiles. Source verification did not establish complete CAMA-negative status, a valid Ph-like classifier, diagnostic timing of all molecular samples, or alignment of the exported survival clock with MRD sampling. CAMA rules were outcome-informed, and the original fully adjusted model had coding and estimation problems. Accordingly, historical HRs and C-index differences are disclosed for reproducibility but are not retained as valid prognostic estimates. The clinical-molecular research framework is retained as the study question; joint survival stratification and incremental discrimination are not established by this dataset.

papers.abstract: Engraftment syndrome (ES) is a clinically challenging, hyper-inflammatory complication following autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT). The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) has emerged as a reliable biomarker for endothelial dysfunction and non-relapse mortality in allogeneic transplantation; however, its predictive utility for ES in the autologous setting has not been fully established. This study evaluated the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of ES in patients with multiple myeloma (MM) and lymphoma, focusing on the dynamic predictive value of peritransplant EASIX scores. We retrospectively analyzed 303 adult patients with MM or lymphoma who underwent ASCT at a single center between 2015 and 2025. ES was diagnosed using the Maiolino criteria. EASIX was assessed at four time points: before conditioning, on the day of transplantation (day 0), and on days +7 and +14. The incidence of ES was 14.2%. Demographic characteristics, conditioning regimens, and infused cell doses did not differ significantly between patients with and without ES. Pre-conditioning EASIX scores were comparable between groups; however, the median EASIX score on day 0 was significantly higher in patients who subsequently developed ES (2.35 vs. 1.46; p = 0.019). In univariable logistic regression, log-transformed EASIX on day 0 was associated with ES development (OR 1.399, 95% CI 1.033-1.894), with an AUC of 0.612 (95% CI 0.524-0.700). Patients with ES had a significantly higher rate of severe (grade 3-4) diarrhea (48.8% vs. 23.1%) and prolonged post-transplant antibiotic therapy (median 12 vs. 8 days). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in progression-free or overall survival. In conclusion, engraftment syndrome significantly increases early post-transplant gastrointestinal toxicity and supportive care requirements without adversely affecting long-term survival outcomes. While log-transformed EASIX on day 0 correlates with ES risk, its standalone discriminative performance remains modest. EASIX is best utilized as an integrated component within broader, multiparametric risk-stratification models rather than as an isolated predictor.

papers.abstract: To characterize genomic and transcriptomic features associated with established clinicopathologic risk categories in patients with dysplasia and early gastric cancer (EGC) undergoing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and to explore molecular correlates of noncurative resection and metachronous recurrence. A prospective cohort study was conducted involving 99 patients with EGC or dysplasia who underwent ESD at a tertiary care center. Pre-ESD biopsy samples were subjected to whole-exome sequencing (WES) and whole-transcriptome sequencing (WTS). Clinicopathologic data and molecular profiles were analyzed to identify molecular features associated with curative resection and metachronous recurrence. Of the 99 patients enrolled in the study, 85 were diagnosed with early gastric cancer (EGC) and 14 with dysplasia. Among the 85 patients, 43 (50.6%) met absolute curative criteria, 28 (32.9%) met expanded criteria, and 14 (16.5%) were classified as noncurative. Genomic analysis revealed distinct mutation patterns associated with clinicopathologic risk categories, including recurrent mutations in KRAS and TP53. Transcriptomic profiling identified 186 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) related to noncurative resection, with enrichment in pathways involving extracellular matrix remodeling, immune signaling, and cell migration. Metachronous recurrence occurred in 6 of the 85 patients (7.1%). Exploratory transcriptomic analyses identified enrichment of inflammatory and immune-related pathways, including NF-κB and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling in tumors from patients who subsequently developed metachronous recurrence. Diffuse-type EGC showed enhanced epithelial-mesenchymal transition and matrix remodeling compared to intestinal type. Integrating genomic and transcriptomic data with clinicopathologic features provides additional insight into the molecular characteristics associated with established risk categories in EGC. These findings expand our understanding of the molecular heterogeneity of EGC and provide a foundation for future studies evaluating the clinical utility of molecular profiling in larger independent cohorts.

papers.abstract: This study investigated the role of p300-associated Yin Yang 1 (YY1) lactylation in glycolytic reprogramming and malignant phenotypes of glioblastoma (GBM) cells. Immunohistochemical analysis of a GBM tissue microarray revealed stronger p300 staining in GBM tissues than in normal brain tissues. In U251 cells, p300 overexpression enhanced cell viability, colony formation, migration, and invasion while reducing apoptosis, whereas p300 knockdown produced opposite effects. Metabolic analyses further showed that increased p300 expression was associated with enhanced glucose uptake, lactate production, extracellular acidification rate (ECAR), and intracellular ATP levels, together with reduced oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and increased expression of glycolysis-related proteins, including hexokinase 2 (HK2), phosphofructokinase 2 (PFK2), and glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1). Co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence analyses supported an association and nuclear colocalization between p300 and YY1. Peptide-based antibody validation and immunoprecipitation assays further supported the presence of YY1 lactylation, while modulation of p300 expression was associated with changes in YY1 lactylation levels. Functional comparisons between wild-type YY1 (YY1-WT) and the K183R mutant showed that the mutation was associated with reduced YY1 lactylation signals, attenuated glycolytic activity, and less aggressive cellular phenotypes in U251 cells. Further analyses in both U251 and U-87 MG cells indicated that YY1-WT was associated with increased YY1 enrichment at the HK2 promoter and enhanced HK2 promoter reporter activity, whereas these effects were attenuated by the K183R substitution. Overexpression of HK2 in the YY1-K183R background partially or substantially reversed the associated changes in HK2 expression, glycolytic metabolism, and malignant cellular phenotypes. Collectively, these findings support a role for the p300-YY1-HK2 regulatory axis in linking YY1 lactylation-associated changes to glycolytic reprogramming and malignant phenotypes in GBM cells.

papers.abstract: Serum amyloid A (SAA), an acute-phase protein reflecting systemic inflammatory status, may provide prognostic information in patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving immunotherapy. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic stratification value of baseline SAA in patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. We retrospectively analyzed 87 patients with advanced gastric cancer who received PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based therapy at Zhejiang Cancer Hospital between June 2019 and July 2023. Baseline SAA, C-reactive protein (CRP), albumin (ALB), and clinical characteristics were collected at treatment initiation. Optimal cut-off values were determined using X-tile analysis. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression models. The optimal cut-off value for baseline SAA was 13 mg/L. Compared with patients with SAA > 13 mg/L, those with SAA ≤ 13 mg/L had significantly longer overall survival (OS) (15.8 vs. 10.8 months, p = 0.004) and a lower risk of death (HR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.33-0.81). Progression-free survival (PFS) was also improved in the SAA ≤ 13 mg/L group (HR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.33-0.85; log-rank p = 0.007). No significant difference was observed in Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1-based treatment response between groups. Patients with SAA > 13 mg/L showed higher CRP levels and lower ALB levels (both p < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, peritoneal metastasis and prior radical gastrectomy remained independently associated with OS, whereas SAA lost statistical significance after adjustment. Elevated baseline SAA was associated with poorer OS and PFS in patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. SAA may reflect systemic inflammatory-host status and serve as an accessible biomarker for prognostic risk stratification, although prospective validation is required.

papers.abstract: Mobile clinics may be an opportune mechanism for delivering cancer genetic testing to underserved populations. This study sought to characterize current workflows and patient journeys in a mobile mammography program and to understand patient attitudes toward genetic testing, cancer risk, and digital health tools. Iterative multi-modal qualitative data collection via structured interviews with patients and providers (n = 42) and observations (96 h) of mobile clinic visits to community health centers, regional health fairs and a community-based organization. We describe patient journeys varying by the patient's referral source and usual source of care. Patients are unfamiliar with genetic testing but are open to it and concerned about cancer risk. They are aware of the value of family history in identifying heightened cancer risk but vary in their ability to provide it. Patients described relying on assistance from others to use digital tools, distrusting online health information, and preferring to receive information from trusted medical sources. Our findings suggest that the population is receptive to genetic testing and interested in trustworthy alternatives to online health information. The population is in need of tailored patient education and family history elicitation. Concerns about testing cost are a barrier. The feasibility of using digital tools like chatbots to overcome barriers to patient education and family history collection in this context requires further research. If used, chatbots should be provided alongside training, including for family members who may assist some patients in the use of digital technologies. This study informs planning of a novel mobile genetic testing approach for hereditary cancer risk, responding directly to the needs of a population with well-known disparities.

papers.abstract: The burden of cervical cancer is disproportionately high in sub-Saharan Africa. We examined whether mental disorders contribute to cervical cancer-related disparities in South Africa, analysing medical claims data from an insurance scheme between 2011 and 2020. Using Cox proportional hazards models, we computed adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for the association between various types of mental disorders and the incidence of cervical pre-cancer and cancer compared to women without any mental disorder. We included 568,408 women in the analysis of cervical pre-cancer and 567,984 in the analysis of cervical cancer. A total of 15,062 women had an incident cervical pre-cancer diagnosis (722.0/100 000 person-years, 95% confidence interval [CI] 710.6-733.7) and 653 a cervical cancer diagnosis (30.7/100,000 person-years, 95% CI 28.4-33.2). Women with any mental disorder diagnosis were more likely to be diagnosed with cervical pre-cancer (aHR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.10) but less likely to be diagnosed with cervical cancer (aHR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51-0.75). Similarly, women with depression (aHR 1.10, 95% CI 1.05-1.16) or bipolar disorder (aHR 1.15, 95% CI 1.01-1.39) were more likely to be diagnosed with cervical pre-cancer than women without any mental disorder, but less likely to have a cervical cancer diagnosis. Anxiety was also associated with lower cervical cancer diagnosis rates (adjusted HR 0.61, 95%CI 0.46-0.81). Our findings highlight the complex interplay between mental health, health care access, and cervical cancer risk and underscore the necessity of research to inform equitable cervical cancer prevention for women with and without mental disorders in South Africa.

papers.abstract: Metastasis remains the leading cause of mortality in prostate cancer (PCa). Loss-of-function mutations in SPOP, commonly observed in metastatic PCa, have undefined roles in the metastatic niche. Histone methyltransferase ASH1L plays a crucial role in leukemogenesis and is overexpressed in various solid tumors. However, its post-translational regulation and protein homeostasis in cancer remain poorly understood. Here, we report that SPOP mutations promote PCa lung metastasis and induce infiltration of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in graft models. We identified that the CUL3-SPOP E3 ubiquitin ligase complex is a key regulator of ASH1L protein, mediating its polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. PCa-associated SPOP mutations cause aberrant stabilization of ASH1L, thereby epigenetically activating the oncogenic glycoprotein MUC1. Dysregulation of the ASH1L-MUC1 axis augmented CD133-associated cancer stemness and TAM recruitment in the metastatic niche. In preclinical models, genetic knockdown of ASH1L or pharmacological inhibition of MUC1 significantly suppressed lung metastasis driven by SPOP mutations. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized SPOP-ASH1L-MUC1-CD133 regulatory axis linking genetic alterations to metastatic niche remodeling and reveal actionable vulnerabilities in metastatic PCa. It uncovers novel post-translational regulation of pro-metastatic epigenetic factor ASH1L and informs biomarker-guided MUC1-targeted therapy for metastatic PCa.

papers.abstract: Cancer is associated with metabolic disorders, yet the impact of endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (ENMs) on cancer remains unclear. Here, we show the associations of 25 ENMs with cancer trajectories, from primary cancer incidence to multi-primary cancers and mortality, using a multi-state model in a prospective cohort of 405,023 participants. Our findings reveal heterogeneous associations of ENMs across cancer sites and types, identifying 8 cancer-related ENMs that define four subtypes: C1 (iron deficiency/metabolism disorders dominated), C2 (type 2 diabetes dominated), C3 (lipid/lipoprotein metabolism disorders dominated), and C4 (osteoporosis dominated). Subtype-specific and subtype-shared proteomic mediators are identified and their contributions are quantified, with RNASET2 emerging as the major shared mediator. Furthermore, a deep-learning model integrating ENM subtypes and mediators enables personalized prediction of cancer incidence (AUCs = 0.80-0.90) and performs better than conventional Cox models. Our findings highlight the relevance of ENMs to cancer risk, providing mechanistic insights into metabolism-associated tumorigenesis.

papers.abstract: Accurate and minimally invasive percutaneous biopsy is critical for early lung cancer diagnosis, yet conventional manual procedures suffer from repeated radiation exposure, high reliance on doctor expertise, and risk of tissue injury. This study presents a 5 degree-of-freedom robotic system combined with an intelligent shared control framework guided by expert skills learning. Expert skills were modeled using a variational autoencoder-hidden Markov model to segment latent procedural phases, and dynamic motion primitives reconstructed representative expert trajectories. These learned skills were integrated into a phase-adaptive shared controller, enabling online modulation of impedance and trajectory parameters. Both phantom and in vivo porcine experiments validated the system's feasibility, safety, and accuracy, with animal experiment studies confirming minimal tissue trauma and stable physiological responses. Compared with manual, leader-follower, and admittance control methods, the intelligent shared control substantially reduced force fluctuations and trajectory deviations.

papers.abstract: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria. Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims. None.

papers.abstract: Dietary therapy, the gut microbiota, and immune responses interact in complex ways. Our study demonstrates that a ketogenic diet (KD) enhances the efficacy of an anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (anti-PD-1) monoclonal antibody in colorectal cancer (CRC). Integrated microbiome and metabolome analyses revealed a marked increase in the abundance of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA)-producing bacteria, along with elevated levels of their metabolic products, the BCAAs, in the combination treatment group. Furthermore, exogenous BCAA supplementation improved the anti-tumor efficacy of anti-PD-1. Mechanistically, BCAAs maintain the proteostasis of the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) in CRC by promoting its K63-linked ubiquitination and inhibiting K48-linked ubiquitination-mediated proteasomal degradation, thereby activating the interferon-β (IFN-β) pathway within the tumor microenvironment (TME) to enhance anti-tumor CD8+ T cell immunity. In patients with metastatic CRC (mCRC) receiving immunotherapy, BCAA levels and the STING-IFN-β axis were associated with prognosis. These findings provide a theoretical and practical rationale for combining dietary modulation with immune-based therapies in the clinical management of CRC.

papers.abstract: LTBP4 loss promotes colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but its role in tumor angiogenesis remains undefined. Here, we report that LTBP4 deficiency drives intratumoral angiogenesis in CRC. In murine CRC models, Ltbp4-knockout tumors exhibited increased vessel density and reduced blood oxygen saturation compared with wild-type controls. Consistent with these observations, LTBP4 expression in human CRC tissues inversely correlated with vessel junctions and total vessel area. Functional assays further confirmed that conditioned medium from LTBP4-knockdown CRC cells promoted endothelial tube formation, migration, and proliferation, whereas LTBP4 overexpression suppressed these effects. Mechanistically, LTBP4 deficiency increased active TGF-β1 levels and reduced TSP1 expression through the BMP4/SMAD5 axis, both of which contributed to enhanced endothelial angiogenic responses. Therapeutically, administration of recombinant TSP1 to Ltbp4-deficient tumors promoted vascular normalization, as evidenced by increased pericyte coverage, improved perfusion, and reduced hypoxia. TSP1 treatment also enhanced the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy, which was associated with increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration and a shift towards M1-like macrophage polarization. In clinical CRC cohorts, concurrent low expression of LTBP4 and TSP1 identified a patient subgroup with vascular abnormalities, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and poor prognosis. Collectively, our findings establish an LTBP4-BMP4-SMAD5-TSP1 regulatory axis that links angiogenesis with immune modulation in CRC, and suggest that this axis may serve as a prognostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target for vascular normalization to improve immunotherapy response.

papers.abstract: Phosphorylation dysregulation is a marker of cancer serving as a key mechanism for tumor malignant progression. However, the mechanism by which the phosphorylation of metabolic enzymes drives metastasis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. Here, we identify phosphorylation of stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD) at serine 198 (pSCD) as a key driver of metastasis in ESCC. Analysis of clinical phosphoproteomic datasets revealed elevated pSCD levels correlating with ESCC metastasis. Functional assays demonstrated that pSCD promotes ESCC metastasis independently of SCD's desaturase activity. pSCD translocates into the nucleus, where it directly binds to the scaffold protein MTA2 within the NuRD complex, suppressing deacetylase activity and reprogramming transcription toward pro-metastatic programs. Integrative ATAC-seq and RNA-seq analyses identified increased accessibility and expression of metastasis-related genes, including MET, KDR, PGF, FGF5, FGF18, and IGF1R. Mechanistically, p110α mediates the phosphorylation of SCD S198, enhancing KPNA2-dependent nuclear import by exposing the nuclear localization signal of SCD through conformational changes. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized PI3K-pSCD-MTA2/NuRD signaling axis that links the phosphorylation of metabolic enzymes to chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation, thereby driving ESCC metastasis.

papers.abstract: Imbalance in copper ion homeostasis is closely associated with the development and progression of various cancers, yet its dynamic regulatory mechanisms and targeting value in colorectal cancer remain unclear. This study reveals the relationship between endogenous metabolites and copper-dependent proliferation in CRC, identifying the histone deacetylase SIRT6 as a critical hub regulating copper homeostasis and determining cell fate. SIRT6 knockout promotes copper-dependent proliferation but simultaneously sensitizes CRC cells to cuproptosis. Mechanistically, SIRT6 epigenetically suppresses the transcription of SLC31A1 by deacetylating H3K9/K56, thereby limiting intracellular copper accumulation and inhibiting cuproplasia. On the other hand, SIRT6 directly binds to and deacetylates the transcription factor MTF1, inhibiting its ubiquitination-mediated degradation and enhancing its transcriptional activity, consequently promoting the expression of metallothioneins. MT1A/MT2A remodel subcellular copper distribution through copper chelation, reducing mitochondrial copper load and conferring resistance to cuproptosis. Importantly, the combined application of the SIRT6 inhibitor OSS_128167 and the copper ionophore Elesclomol demonstrated significant synergistic anti-tumor efficacy in patient-derived xenograft models. This study discovers and elucidates the novel function of SIRT6 as a master regulator of copper metabolism, redefines the high-copper tumor microenvironment as a targetable metabolic vulnerability, and provides a new theoretical foundation and a highly promising combination therapy strategy for the precision treatment of colorectal cancer.

papers.abstract: Radical nephroureterectomy is the standard treatment for patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma, but causes irreversible nephron loss and can limit subsequent systemic therapy. We aimed to assess a response-adapted kidney-preserving strategy integrating induction disitamab vedotin plus tislelizumab, selective kidney-sparing surgery, and longitudinal circulating tumour DNA and urinary tumour DNA monitoring in patients with localised high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma. DISTINCT-I was a single-arm, phase 2 trial conducted at two tertiary referral centres in China. Adults aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed, localised, high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma (cT1-T3, N0-N1, M0), and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2 received 2·0 mg/kg intravenous disitamab vedotin plus intravenous 200 mg tislelizumab once every 3 weeks for two to four cycles, followed by response-adapted kidney-sparing surgery when feasible. The primary endpoint was the 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival rate, assessed in the intention-to-treat population. Kidney-intact event-free survival was defined as the time from enrolment to the earliest occurrence of high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma recurrence, death from any cause, or conversion to radical nephroureterectomy. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events and Clavien-Dindo classification. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05912816), and is ongoing. Between Sept 6, 2023, and Nov 15, 2024, 36 patients were assessed for eligibility; ten did not meet the eligibility criteria and six declined to participate. Of the 20 patients enrolled, 17 (85%) were male and three (15%) were female; all patients were Chinese. At data cutoff (Dec 31, 2025), median follow-up was 17·0 months (IQR 14·0-23·0). The 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival rate was 70% (95% CI 46-88; 14 participants). Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (10%) patients (fatigue in one and increased γ-glutamyl transferase in another). No grade 4-5 treatment-related adverse events, serious treatment-related adverse events, or treatment-related deaths occurred. This structured, multimodal, response-adapted strategy was associated with kidney preservation in selected patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma. These findings support further prospective comparative evaluation of organ-preserving strategies in patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma. papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) analysis has become a cornerstone in dissecting single-cell and spatial omics data, having an indispensable role in high-throughput screening and comprehensive characterization of tissue communication landscapes. Computational models and analytical objectives have emerged continuously in recent years, propelling CCC methodology development and leading to unprecedented biological discoveries. Methodological varieties and differences in their characteristics underscore the urgent need for a coherent framework bridging between CCC biology and computational advances. Here, we systematically curate 161 published CCC methods, classifying them hierarchically into two primary categories and nine subcategories based on their functions and model features and highlighting the power of CCC methods using oncology examples. Four directions for future CCC methodology development are presented, emphasizing AI-biology integration. This Review aims to delineate the CCC algorithm-demand landscape, thereby fostering comprehensive, in-depth and reliable elucidation of CCC and facilitating broad applications in biology and disease studies.

papers.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is effective in both HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancers, but clinical responses are heterogeneous. To delineate spatial determinants of response, we perform spatial transcriptomics in patients treated with T-DXd. More spatially dispersed HER2 expression in cancer cells correlates with improved response, consistent with the bystander effect. In HER2-positive tumors, resistant fragments show downregulation of ERBB2 expression and activation of PI3K and EGFR pathways, with possible involvement of autocrine amphiregulin-EGFR signaling. In HER2-low tumors, resistance is associated with pharmacokinetic barriers: resistant fragments exhibit increased cancer-to-vessel distance, reduced colocalization of HER2 with cathepsin linker-cleaving enzymes, and diminished predicted peritumoral payload concentration. Exploratory longitudinal analyses of paired pre-treatment and post-progression samples reveal increased cancer-to-vessel distance at resistance. Our study identifies spatial features associated with ADC response and resistance in clinical samples and provides a rationale for further investigation of candidate determinants.

papers.abstract: Socioeconomic deprivation is a key determinant of health inequity. In a recent UK-based observational study, more socioeconomically deprived elective patients undergoing surgery were reported to have poorer baseline health despite presenting for surgery at a younger age. This study highlights potentially modifiable demographic characteristics and health behaviours. However, before these observations can be used to inform clinical decision-making and policy change, the complex multifactorial nature of these exposure-outcome relationships must be delineated. This includes accounting for the duration of exposure to components that drive social and economic disadvantage, differences across nations and over time, intersectionality, and the low representation of highly deprived and minority ethnic groups.

papers.abstract: Germline mutations in PARN cause dyskeratosis congenita (DC), an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome characterized by multilineage cytopenia and progression to myeloid disease. The mechanisms underlying this malignant transformation have not been fully elucidated. Here we show, using a loss-of-function CRISPR-Cas9 zebrafish parn mutant, hematopoietic stem and progenitor (HSPC) expansion and reduced mature hematopoietic cells across various lineages. Cholesterol biosynthesis was transcriptionally activated; a finding recapitulated in patient-derived iPSCs with PARN mutations. Inhibiting cholesterol biosynthesis rescued HSPC expansion and anemia in parn mutants. Concurrent myeloid differentiation therapy or Wnt inhibition reduced HSPCs to varying degrees. We further demonstrate a role for activated Erk signaling in impairing erythrocyte differentiation and show robust rescue with trametinib treatment. Overall, our findings uncover unrecognized roles for Parn in regulating cholesterol metabolism and Erk signaling and provide preclinical evidence for targeting these pathways to restore hematopoiesis in DC.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

papers.abstract: Immune cell plasticity is a defining feature of tumor immunity and is increasingly recognized as being governed by epigenetic regulation. Advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics have uncovered an epigenetic checkpoint that integrates environmental cues within the tumor microenvironment (TME) to shape immune cell fate and function. In this review, we synthesize recent evidence supporting three interconnected paradigms of epigenetic control in tumor immunity from the perspective of immune cell heterogeneity, ecology, and state transitions. First, dynamic chromatin remodeling programs myeloid cell polarization and functional diversification. Second, epitranscriptomic regulation constrains T and B cell states, contributing to immune dysfunction and exhaustion. Third, spatially resolved epigenetic remodeling influences immune cell trafficking, positioning, and retention within tumors. Collectively, these mechanisms establish durable immune states that reinforce TME-driven immunosuppression. We further highlight emerging pharmacological strategies targeting epigenetic regulators to reprogram immune cell function and enhance anti-tumor immunity. This framework provides a foundation for leveraging epigenetic plasticity to improve the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Etomidate is commonly used for induction in hemodynamically unstable patients to preserve cardiovascular stability. However, concerns persist regarding potential adverse outcomes, including adrenal suppression and increased mortality. We evaluated whether intravenous anesthetic induction with etomidate was independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes as compared to propofol induction. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 155,667 adult surgical patients undergoing induction with etomidate or propofol at our academic health system. Patients younger than 18 years of age, those receiving preoperative mechanical ventilation, and those with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status VI were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes included sepsis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), cardiogenic shock, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and surgical factors. Given substantial baseline imbalance between induction groups, propensity score matching (1:1) using the same covariates was performed. Sensitivity analyses included adjustment for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, complete-case analyses, and interaction testing. A total of 155,667 patients met inclusion criteria, including 3846 (2.5%) who received etomidate and 151,821 (97.5%) who received propofol. Thirty-day mortality occurred in 1151 patients (0.74%). Unadjusted mortality was higher in the etomidate group (227/3846 [5.9%]) than in the propofol group (924/151,821 [0.61%]). After multivariable adjustment, etomidate use remained independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (aOR 1.44; 95% CI, 1.21-1.72; P < 0.001). Propensity score matching (n = 3832 per group) reduced the average standardized mean difference from 0.398 before matching to 0.023 after matching. The association persisted in the matched cohort (aOR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.14-1.78; P = 0.002), with observed mortality of 225/3832 (5.9%) among etomidate recipients and 157/3832 (4.1%) among propofol recipients, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 1.8% and a number needed to harm of 56. In the matched cohort, etomidate was also associated with higher odds of sepsis (aOR 1.28; 95% CI, 1.08-1.52), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.09-1.41), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.56; 95% CI, 1.21-2.01), and acute kidney injury (aOR 1.27; 95% CI, 1.11-1.45). Post-induction hypotension was lower in the etomidate group (aOR 0.40, 95% CI 0.32-0.49; P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Etomidate induction was associated with increased 30-day mortality and major postoperative complications. Given the observational design, results should be interpreted with caution.
