papers.abstract: The use of Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) in medically directed anesthesia care teams has expanded, but the implications for anesthesia time and billing units remain uncertain, especially in relation to staffing supervision ratios (number of CRNAs to anesthesiologist). We conducted a retrospective fixed-panel observational study of unique surgical encounters spanning January 2018 through December 2024 using billing records from a large revenue cycle management company. The sample included encounters involving anesthesiologists, CRNAs, surgeons, and facilities across 47 states. We compared physician-alone cases with medically directed care-team cases using fixed-effects regression models. Outcomes included anesthesia minutes and anesthesia billing units (base, time, modifier, conditional, and total units). A Medicare subsample was analyzed for realized gross payments. Secondary analyses examined each encounter by the number of CRNAs the anesthesiologist medically directed simultaneously, that is, staffing ratios, to assess whether outcomes varied by level. Models adjusted for patient-, procedure-, surgeon-, facility-, and time-level factors. Care-team cases were associated with longer anesthesia time (adjusted difference +1.67 minutes; 95% CI, 1.11-2.23; P < .001) and higher total billing units (adjusted difference +0.11 units; 95% CI, 0.04-0.18; P = .003) than cases performed by an anesthesiologist alone. Both differences increased with the staffing ratio. Relative to physician-alone cases, anesthesia time was shorter with 1 CRNA directed (-2.52 minutes; 95% CI, -3.22 to -1.83), similar with 2 CRNAs (-0.13 minutes; 95% CI, -0.69 to 0.43), and longer with 3 CRNAs (+3.03 minutes; 95% CI, 2.40-3.66) and 4 CRNAs (+6.99 minutes; 95% CI, 6.18-7.80); total billing units followed the same pattern (1 CRNA, -0.23; 2 CRNAs, -0.02 [not significant]; 3 CRNAs, +0.21; 4 CRNAs, +0.50). In a Medicare subsample, gross payments differed little overall (-$3.53; 95% CI, -$5.13 to -$1.92) and followed the same staffing-ratio gradient (1 CRNA, -$10.44; 4 CRNAs, +$3.74). Medically directed CRNA care teams were associated with modestly longer anesthesia time and slightly greater billing-unit intensity than physician-alone care. These differences were small overall but increased with rising staffing ratios, indicating that the number of CRNAs directed concurrently is associated with measurable differences in anesthesia time and billing intensity.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative haemodynamic monitoring primarily targets arterial pressure and flow but might not adequately reflect tissue perfusion. The peripheral perfusion index provides a continuous, noninvasive, and readily available indicator of peripheral perfusion, but its prognostic significance across surgical populations remains uncertain. We hypothesised that greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index would be associated with postoperative complications and mortality. In this prespecified multicentre cohort study using electronic health record data, we included adults (≥18 yr) undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery. The primary exposure was cumulative intraoperative area under a perfusion index of 1.5 expressed in PI⋅min. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The secondary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative intensive care unit admission, reoperation, acute kidney injury, or prolonged hospital stay. Among 399 842 patients undergoing 540 101 procedures, a total of 7066 (1.3%) deaths occurred within 30 days: 654 (0.5%) among procedures with no exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min). Compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at the 95th percentile of exposure (42.5 PI⋅min), with similar patterns observed across the major surgical specialties. For the composite outcome, the corresponding odds ratio was 1.16 (95% CI 1.14-1.18; P<0.001). Greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index was associated with higher postoperative mortality and complications in adult patients undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery. papers.abstract: Electronic cigarette aerosols may promote airway inflammation, bronchial hyperreactivity, and impaired mucociliary defence, but their perioperative respiratory safety remains uncertain. We examined whether preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence. We conducted a nationwide matched cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network database, comparing surgical patients with documented preoperative vaping-related disorder and cigarette nicotine dependence. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative respiratory complications, including pneumonia, respiratory failure, bronchospasm, noninvasive ventilation, and mechanical ventilation. Among 3817 matched pairs, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of 30-day respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence (10.7% vs 5.1%, relative risk [RR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.79-2.49). Vaping-related disorder was also associated with increased risks of pneumonia (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.40-4.28), respiratory failure (RR 2.48, 95% CI 1.98-3.10), bronchospasm (RR 1.92, 95% CI, 1.38-2.68), and noninvasive ventilation (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.64-3.98). Vaping-related disorder combined with cigarette nicotine dependence was associated with a higher risk of respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence alone (RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53), whereas vaping-related disorder alone showed a larger RR increase than neither diagnosis (RR 3.11, 95% CI 2.56-3.76). Among surgical patients, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence. These findings suggest that vaping history should be specifically assessed during preoperative evaluation and considered in perioperative respiratory risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Advanced age is a major risk factor for both delirium and dementia. A potential early biomarker for dementia is the brain-predicted age difference (brainPAD). We hypothesised that brain ageing accelerates after postoperative delirium (POD), and that increased brainPAD is associated with cognitive decline. Brain MRI scans were obtained in 287 older patients before and 3 months after major elective surgery, and two MRI scans at similar time intervals were obtained in 46 nonsurgical control participants. We computed grey matter brainPAD in patients with POD (POD+), patients without POD (POD-), and nonsurgical controls. The Trail Making Test (TMT) was administered at both time points to examine associations between changes in brainPAD and changes in attention/processing speed (TMT-A) and executive task switching (TMT-B and TMT B-A). Compared with the POD- group, brainPAD increased by an additional 6 (sd=3) months over time in the POD+ group (P=0.002). For each 1 year-over-year increase in brain age gap, patients took 2.3 s longer to complete the TMT-A (P=0.016), whereas no association was observed with TMT-B (P=0.254) or TMT B-A (P=0.91). Postoperativ edelirium is associated with accelerated brain ageing, which in turn is associated with decline in attention and processing speed. These findings help to understand the complex relationship between ageing, delirium, and dementia. NCT02265263.

papers.abstract: Radiotherapy to the prostate and pelvic lymph nodes compared with prostate-only radiotherapy has shown benefits for high-risk prostate cancer in some studies, but evidence remains unclear. In low-risk or intermediate-risk disease, prostate-only stereotactic body radiotherapy (P-SBRT) is safe and effective. PACE-NODES aims to demonstrate safety and efficacy of prostate and pelvic nodal SBRT (PPN-SBRT) for high-risk disease. PACE-NODES is a phase 3, open-label, randomised trial conducted at 47 hospitals in the UK, Ireland, and New Zealand. The trial recruited men aged 18 years or older, with a WHO performance status of 0-2, and with high-risk (Gleason score 8-10, stage T3a-T4, or prostate-specific antigen >20 ng/mL), localised prostate adenocarcinoma, planned for at least 12 months of hormone therapy. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1), using minimisation with a random element, to P-SBRT (36·25 Gy prostate) or PPN-SBRT (36·25 Gy prostate, 25 Gy pelvic nodes) in five fractions, on alternate days. Neither participants nor researchers were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint is time to biochemical or clinical failure (not yet mature). This preplanned safety analysis is on secondary endpoints, with a focus on Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade 2 or worse gastrointestinal and genitourinary adverse events within 12 weeks of treatment, analysed by treatment received. Patient-reported outcomes include Expanded Prostate Index Composite Short Form (EPIC-26), International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), and EQ-5D-5L. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05613023) and is ongoing. Between Sept 9, 2022, and July 31, 2025, 1166 participants were recruited and randomly assigned (583 per group). The median age was 72·7 years (IQR 67·7-76·5). 18 patients did not receive radiotherapy; a further 60 (17 assigned to P-SBRT, 43 assigned to PPN-SBRT) did not receive allocated radiotherapy, mostly where planning constraints were not met. This analysis includes 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 511 patients receiving PPN-SBRT who had completed acute follow-up. Median follow-up was 13·8 months (IQR 7·8-21·0). 118 (21·3%) of 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 143 (28·0%) of 511 receiving PPN-SBRT had grade 2 or worse gastrointestinal events within 12 weeks (difference 6·7 percentage points [95% CI 1·6-11·9]; p=0·011; odds ratio [OR] 1·44 [95% CI 1·09-1·91]). This included grade 3 events in eight (1·4%) patients treated with P-SBRT and 11 (2·2%) treated with PPN-SBRT, and a grade 4 event in one (0·2%) patient treated with P-SBRT. 223 (40·2%) of 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 183 (35·8%) of 511 receiving PPN-SBRT had grade 2 or worse genitourinary events (difference -4·4 percentage points [-10·2 to 1·5]; p=0·14; OR 0·83 [0·65-1·06]). This included grade 3 events in seven (1·3%) patients treated with P-SBRT and two (0·4%) treated with PPN-SBRT (no grade 4 events). Genitourinary and gastrointestinal adverse events peaked at 2 weeks and were low and similar between groups at 12 weeks. There were no treatment-related deaths. More patients receiving PPN-SBRT had important decreases in bowel function on 4-week EPIC-26 (208 [54·9%] of 379 receiving P-SBRT, 239 [65·5%] of 365 receiving PPN-SBRT). The proportion of patients reporting moderate or severe urinary symptoms on IPSS at 4 weeks was similar in those receiving P-SBRT (312 [72·4%] of 431) and those receiving PPN-SBRT (284 [71·9%] of 395), as were 4-week decreases in overall health score on EQ-5D-5L (-3·2 [99% CI -4·8 to -1·6] for P-SBRT and -2·5 [-4·1 to -0·9] for PPN-SBRT). P-SBRT and PPN-SBRT for patients with high-risk prostate cancer were deliverable in an international multicentre trial. PPN-SBRT increased gastrointestinal but not genitourinary adverse events. Side-effects diminished rapidly, with no difference by 12 weeks. Follow-up continues for late adverse events and cancer control, which are essential for confirming a role for PPN-SBRT in this setting. Prostate Cancer UK.

papers.abstract: Foundation models are advancing computational pathology by transferring knowledge from large datasets to diagnostic, prognostic and treatment response tasks. Most existing models, however, either operate at the patch level or learn slide-level representations using image-based objectives, coarse tissue labels or pathology reports that vary across institutions and reflect the subjectivity inherent in narrative reporting. Here we introduce THREADS, which instead learns general-purpose whole-slide representations by aligning tissue morphology with genomic or transcriptomic profiles. THREADS was pretrained on over 47,000 hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained tissue sections and evaluated across 107 oncology tasks spanning cancer subtyping and grading, tumor microenvironment characterization, treatment response prediction and survival analysis. THREADS consistently outperformed leading whole-slide foundation models and supervised baselines while demonstrating strong transfer across external cohorts and high label efficiency. These findings establish molecularly guided pretraining as an effective strategy for learning general-purpose whole-slide representations and motivate future extensions incorporating additional molecular, spatial and clinical modalities.

papers.abstract: Postoperative complications remain a leading cause of mortality. Experimental data indicate that roxadustat, a first-in-class prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, reduces ischaemia-reperfusion injury, accelerates wound healing, and enhances survival in sepsis. Therefore, preoperative administration of roxadustat might reduce perioperative organ injury. We examined the perioperative tolerability and the potential for adverse surgical interactions with roxadustat. In this phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind, randomised-controlled pilot trial, 150 patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery were allocated to preoperative roxadustat 100 mg or placebo for three alternate-day doses, with the last dose on the operative morning. The co-primary outcomes were preoperative adverse events and postoperative complications meeting standardised endpoint definitions within 30 days. Among 148 participants (52 [35.1%] females; median age 65 [range 24-84] yr) receiving at least one drug dose, at least one preoperative adverse event occurred in 21 of 75 (28%) in the roxadustat group and 20 of 73 (27%) in the placebo group (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.50-2.12). No serious adverse reactions occurred. Among 143 participants who proceeded to surgery (52 [36.4%] females; median age 65 [range 26-84] yr), ≥1 complication occurred in 23 of 74 participants (31%) who received roxadustat compared with 21 of 69 participants (30%) who received placebo (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.51-2.10). Days alive out of hospital within 30 days was similar between the groups. The annualised enrolment rate was 90 per year, with high levels of drug compliance. Preoperative roxadustat was feasible in patients having major surgery. Uncertainty remains regarding the safety and efficacy of this intervention. www.anzctr.org.au; ACTRN12624000188538.

papers.abstract: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the most common abdominal operation worldwide, yet whether opioid-free anaesthesia improves the overall analgesic benefit remains uncertain. In this multicentre randomised controlled trial, adults undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy were randomised 1:1 to receive opioid-free anaesthesia (dexmedetomidine, esketamine and sevoflurane) or opioid-inclusive anaesthesia (sufentanil and sevoflurane). Patients received prophylactic anti-emetics and multimodal analgesia with flurbiprofen axetil and ropivacaine wound infiltration. The primary outcome was the overall benefit of analgesia score (0-28, lower scores indicate greater benefit) at 24 h postoperatively; a 3-point difference was considered clinically relevant. Secondary outcomes included pain on movement at 24 h and chronic postsurgical pain at 90 days. Between March and September 2025, 315 patients completed this trial (158 opioid-free, 157 opioid-inclusive). The mean (SD) 24-h overall benefit of analgesia score was 2.2 (2.4) after opioid-free anaesthesia vs 3.4 (3.1) after opioid-inclusive anaesthesia (adjusted mean difference -1.3; 95%CI -1.8 to -0.8, p < 0.001), without reaching the threshold for clinical importance. Incidence of pain on movement (adjusted mean difference -0.2; 95%CI -0.4-0) and chronic postsurgical pain (16.1% vs 15.5%; adjusted relative risk 1.03; 95%CI 0.55-1.91) did not differ between groups. Opioid-free anaesthesia was associated with reduced intra-operative hypotension (19.6% vs 35.7%; relative risk 0.55; 95%CI 0.37-0.80) and lower incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (23.4% vs 33.8%; relative risk 0.69; 95%CI 0.48-0.98). Opioid-free anaesthesia did not achieve a clinically meaningful improvement in overall benefit of analgesia. These findings do not support its routine adoption in laparoscopic cholecystectomy. However, the observed reductions in intra-operative hypotension and postoperative nausea and vomiting suggest that this regimen may warrant consideration in selected patients, pending validation in future trials.

papers.abstract: It is common practice to convert an existing labour epidural into surgical anaesthesia for intrapartum caesarean delivery. However, this approach does not always provide adequate anaesthesia. This meta-analysis aimed to determine the incidence of inadequate anaesthesia during epidural conversion for intrapartum caesarean delivery. Databases were searched for observational studies and randomised controlled trials evaluating epidural conversion for intrapartum caesarean delivery. Using a random-effects model and the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation, we calculated the respective incidences of intra-operative patient-reported pain; use of supplemental analgesia; and conversion to general anaesthesia. A total of 43 studies, involving 11,904 patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Pooled incidences of intra-operative pain (eight studies), supplemental analgesia (34 studies) and conversion to general anaesthesia (33 studies) were 20.2% (95%CI 12.2-29.5%, I2 = 93.1%), 17.7% (95%CI 13.3-22.7%, I2 = 96.3%) and 1.3% (95%CI 0.7-2.1%, I2 = 81.7%), respectively. These results were consistent in sensitivity analyses and appeared unaffected by publication year, study design, country type, local anaesthetic used or use of epidural fentanyl. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed due to variability in study methodologies, measurement methods, definitions, thresholds and local clinical practices. This meta-analysis highlights the risk of inadequate anaesthesia and emphasises the importance of thorough pre-operative informed consent when converting labour epidurals to surgical anaesthesia for intrapartum caesarean delivery. However, the considerable heterogeneity in the pooled estimates indicates that these incidences vary significantly across different settings, suggesting that local audit data would be more informative for individual practices.

papers.abstract: Locoregional leptomeningeal metastasis, particularly discrete nodular recurrence after treatment of brain metastases, presents a therapeutic challenge distinct from diffuse leptomeningeal dissemination. Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) may provide focal control of symptomatic or progressive nodules while limiting irradiation of uninvolved tissue. Available retrospective evidence supports feasibility and local radiographic response, but does not establish a survival benefit or protection against distant meningeal progression. Careful distinction among leptomeningeal nodules, dural seeding, and cavity recurrence is essential, as is assessment of the entire neuraxis and cerebrospinal fluid when appropriate. Patient selection should consider lesion distribution, neurologic function, prior irradiation, systemic disease control, and access to central nervous system-active therapies. Focal SRS should complement, rather than replace, comprehensive management of leptomeningeal disease. Prospective multicenter studies should prioritize neurologic function, distant meningeal progression, treatment burden, and patient-centered outcomes to define when local control yields meaningful clinical benefit. A multidisciplinary approach remains central to selecting treatment consistent with each patient's clinical goals.

papers.abstract: Ultrasonic surgical aspirators, including Sonopet®, are widely used during skull base meningioma resection to enable safe tumor debulking in constrained corridors, but aspirated tumor fragments are often discarded. Whether this tissue supports genomic and epigenomic profiling comparable to standard resection tissue is unknown. The aim of this study was to determine whether Sonopet® aspirate is a viable substrate for long-read genomic and epigenomic profiling in skull base meningioma. We prospectively collected paired standard resection (R) and Sonopet® aspirate (S) specimens from seven patients with skull base meningioma and performed Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read whole-genome sequencing using PromethION R10 flow cells. We compared sequencing yield, read quality, tumor purity, copy-number profiles, somatic single-nucleotide variant (SNV) burden, variant allele frequency, and CpG methylation between matched samples, then projected methylation profiles onto a reference framework of 121 EPIC array-profiled samples for molecular group classification. Aspirates generated sequencing yields, read lengths, and tumor purity comparable to matched specimens. Copy-number profiles were largely concordant and recovered canonical meningioma alterations, with close agreement in total and loss burden (Lin's CCC = 0.99, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.00). SNV burden showed moderate agreement (CCC = 0.53, 95% CI - 0.28 to 0.99), with two discordant patients possibly reflecting intratumoral heterogeneity. Promoter methylation was closely correlated between pairs (Pearson r > 0.99 across ~ 177,000 promoters), and molecular group classification was concordant in all pairs except P1, where tumor purity was uncertain. Sonopet® aspirate provides tissue comparable to standard resection specimens for long-read genomic and epigenomic profiling, supporting its use as a substrate for molecular diagnosis and translational research, particularly for subtotally resected tumors with limited tissue.

papers.abstract: Frame-based stereotactic biopsy (STB) lacks intraoperative visual control. Augmented reality (AR) via Microsoft HoloLens 2 offers real-time visualization of the biopsy needle. This study evaluates the technical feasibility and preliminary clinical results of AR navigation during standard frame-based STB. This prospective single-center pilot study included 10 adults undergoing STB for intracranial lesions. Standard trajectory planning utilized the Cosman-Roberts-Wells (CRW®) stereotactic frame, intraoperative computed tomography (CT), and preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in NeuroSight Arc®. Concurrently, Medgital software and HoloLens 2 displayed a hologram of the patient's head, lesion, and trajectory. A passive tracker on the biopsy needle enabled real-time holographic visualization. Endpoints included technical feasibility, registration time, navigation error, diagnostic yield, and complications. AR navigation feasibility was confirmed in all 10 patients (100%). Mean registration time was 79 ± 27 s, and mean AR trajectory error relative to standard planning was 2.21 ± 0.67 mm. A definitive histological diagnosis was obtained in all 10 cases (mean passes: 2.4). No hemorrhagic complications or mortality occurred. Integrating AR navigation (HoloLens 2 and Medgital) with conventional frame-based STB is potentially technically feasible, safe, fast, and provides acceptable accuracy. AR complements the standard workflow by offering direct intraoperative visualization of the needle trajectory.

papers.abstract: Cancer chromosomal instability (CIN) drives tumor evolution through generating structural and numerical chromosome aberrations. However, its molecular determinants remain poorly characterized. Here, we uncover a yet unrecognized role for the tumor suppressor SMAD4 as a key regulator of chromosomal stability. Mechanistically, loss of SMAD4 causes replication stress by promoting transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) and induces subsequent mitotic errors, leading to the concomitant emergence of structural and numerical CIN. While the tumor suppressor function of SMAD4 has been predominantly attributed to transforming growth factor-β signaling, we find that its role in genome maintenance operates via bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and its transcriptional target gene ID3. Consequently, inhibition of BMP signaling mimics the loss of SMAD4, while reexpression of SMAD4 or ID3 in SMAD4-deficient colorectal or pancreatic cancer cells suppresses TRCs, replication stress, and mitotic errors. Our findings reveal a TRC- and replication stress-driven mechanism by which loss of BMP-SMAD4 signaling causes cancer CIN.

papers.abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMDNterm). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMDNterm. Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMDNterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDMENterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

papers.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

papers.abstract: The American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS) classification is widely used, but subjective interpretations cause evaluation variability. Although specific clinical examples were added in 2014 and 2020 to reduce ambiguity, their clinical adoption remains unclear. We evaluated awareness of these examples and whether a multifaceted educational intervention was associated with scoring consistency. This two-phase study evaluated ASA-PS scoring consistency. In Study 1, 45 anesthesiologists at two institutions evaluated 20 simulated adult, pediatric, and obstetric cases to assess understanding of official ASA-PS examples. In Study 2, a pre- and post-intervention study in clinical practice included 414 cases. The intervention included survey feedback, re-dissemination of official examples, and implementation of a reference system in the electronic medical record. The primary outcome was the exact agreement rate between clinician-assigned and consensus scores based on official examples. In Study 1, the overall correct rate with the official reference classifications was 47.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.321). Correct rate was particularly low in pediatric cases (kappa = 0.243). Highly experienced anesthesiologists demonstrated lower correct rates and a tendency toward underestimation. In Study 2, the exact agreement rate increased from 73.5% before the intervention to 82.4% (OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.01-2.78) after the intervention. Cohen's kappa improved from 0.553 to 0.712, and underestimation decreased from 21.1% - 14.8%. Publishing clinical examples alone may be insufficient to standardize ASA-PS classification. A multifaceted intervention incorporating educational feedback and an electronic reference system was associated with improved scoring consistency.

papers.abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 (n = 290), anti-CTLA-4 (n = 175), and combination anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 (n = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 compared to anti-PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti-PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti-PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract: Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), an endogenous lipid mediator, exhibits anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, its efficacy as a stand-alone treatment for acute postoperative pain remains uncertain. This study compared oral micronized PEA with ibuprofen in managing pain following extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL). In this prospective, randomized, double-blind investigation, 120 patients classified as ASA I-II undergoing elective ESWL were evaluated. They were randomly divided to take either 600 mg of oral micronized PEA or 600 mg of ibuprofen two hours prior to the procedure, continuing every 12 h for 72 h. The primary endpoint was postoperative pain intensity quantified by visual analogue scale (VAS) 2 h post-ESWL. Secondary endpoints included VAS scores at predefined intervals, rescue analgesia, adverse events, and patient satisfaction. VAS scores were comparable between groups during the early postoperative period, including at 2 h (PEA: 1 [0-2] vs. ibuprofen: 1 [0-2], P = 0.091). However, pain was significantly higher with PEA at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h (P < 0.001). Rescue analgesia was required more frequently with PEA (76.7% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.032), with greater cumulative opioid consumption (10.7 ± 2.2 vs. 9.4 ± 1.8 mg, P = 0.003). Gastrointestinal discomfort was more frequent with ibuprofen (21.7% vs. 1.7%, P < 0.001). In this active-comparator trial, oral micronized PEA was inferior to ibuprofen at 12-48 h after ESWL, with more rescue analgesia, but early pain scores were similar. The analgesic effect of PEA itself cannot be established. Fewer gastrointestinal adverse events warrant further study.

papers.abstract: The optimal duration of follow-up for patients with follicular lymphoma (FL) eligible for initial watch-and-wait (WAW) remains undefined. We investigated the clinical characteristics and treatment trajectory patterns in patients with FL managed by initial, continuous WAW for at least 5 years (WAW5). Patients were identified from The Danish National Lymphoma Registry and detailed information was collected from health care records. Among the 393 included WAW5-patients, 271 (69%) were still untreated after a median follow-up of 5.3 years (after WAW5-timepoint). The 2-, 5-, and 10-year cumulative incidences of treatment initiation were 16% (95% CI 12%-20%), 28% (95% CI 24%-33%) and 38% (95% CI 32%-44%), respectively. In patients with stage II-IV disease, the best subset selection method in the training cohort (7:3 random sampling) identified the multivariable Cox regression model with number of nodal areas and bone marrow involvement with the best prognostic fit for time to treatment (TTT). Based on this, the WAW5-TTT risk score was constructed. The 5-year cumulative incidence of treatment initiation in the training cohort was 46% (95% CI 35%-58%), 37% (95% CI 26%-48%), and 13% (95% CI 5%-21%) in the high-, intermediate, and low-risk WAW5-TTT groups, respectively (Gray's test p < 0.0001). Results were confirmed in the test cohort. In conclusion, most patients remained treatment-free beyond the WAW5-timepoint. The findings support consideration of discontinuation of routine follow-up or transition to a more flexible, need-driven follow-up after WAW5, with the option of incorporating relevant risk factors to support individualized decision-making.

papers.abstract: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) is a multifunctional protein that participates in cancer metabolism, apoptosis, DNA repair, angiogenesis, and immune regulation beyond its canonical glycolytic role. However, how distinct post-translational modifications (PTMs) coordinate GAPDH functional transitions and determine its diverse biological roles in cancer remains incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize current advances in GAPDH PTMs, including methylation, phosphorylation, acetylation, ubiquitination, S-nitrosylation, serotonylation, crotonylation, lactylation, and succinylation, with emphasis on modification sites, regulatory enzymes, cellular contexts, and functional consequences. We propose a PTM-driven molecular switching model in which different cellular stimuli induce specific GAPDH modifications to regulate its enzymatic activity, subcellular localization, and protein interactions. Representative mechanisms include Src-mediated Tyr41 phosphorylation promoting DNA repair and 5-fluorouracil resistance in colorectal cancer, K254 and K160 acetylation regulating glycolytic activity and apoptosis through distinct cellular contexts, Parkin-mediated ubiquitination controlling mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming, and Gln262 serotonylation enhancing CD8+ T-cell glycolytic function and antitumor immunity. We further discuss the crosstalk among GAPDH PTMs and critically evaluate the current evidence, limitations, and therapeutic implications of GAPDH modification-based regulation. Although GAPDH PTMs represent promising targets for cancer intervention, current evidence is mainly derived from cellular and preclinical models, and PTM-specific therapeutic strategies remain limited. Further studies are required to clarify the cancer-specific functions and clinical relevance of GAPDH PTM networks.

papers.abstract: Influenza viruses and coronaviruses are enveloped, single-stranded RNA viruses that pose persistent and pandemic threats to global public health. Despite belonging to distinct viral families, they share remarkable parallels in modes of transmission, clinical manifestations, and socioeconomic impacts, yet diverge fundamentally in evolutionary mechanisms and epidemiological trajectories. This review compares the history, spread, treatments, and vaccines for these two types of viruses. Influenza viruses possess a segmented genome, which enables antigenic shift and reassortment. In contrast, coronaviruses have large, nonsegmented genomes and rely on recombination, mutation accumulation, and insertions to achieve host switching and immune evasion. Both spread to humans through wildlife (intermediate hosts), live animal markets, intensive agriculture, and global travel. Antiviral strategies have evolved from M2 and neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) for influenza to polymerase inhibitors and protease inhibitors for coronavirus, yet drug resistance remains a common challenge. Vaccine platforms, including inactivated, live-attenuated, recombinant, mRNA, and viral vector technologies, have been deployed against both viruses. This review concludes that integrated, platform-based preparedness, encompassing broad-spectrum antivirals, universal vaccines, and proactive ecological surveillance, is essential for building pandemic-resilient public health systems capable of responding to both influenza and coronavirus threats, as well as future emerging respiratory viruses.

papers.abstract: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during total aortic arch replacement (TAR) is associated with coagulopathy. We investigated whether fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administration during CPB was associated with postoperative transfusion requirements and coagulation profiles after TAR. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective TAR. Patients were categorized according to whether FFP was administered during CPB. The primary outcome was postoperative FFP transfusion from CPB separation to 12 h after intensive care unit admission. Secondary outcomes included perioperative plasma-derived product use, postoperative bleeding, re-exploration for bleeding, and serial coagulation parameters. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders. Data from 156 patients were analyzed, including 111 patients in the Pre-FFP group and 45 in the Control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although deep hypothermic circulatory arrest duration and CPB fluid management differed between the groups. The adjusted mean difference in total post-CPB FFP transfusion units between the Pre-FFP and Control groups was - 1.54 units (95% confidence interval, - 7.51 to 4.43). No significant differences were observed in perioperative plasma-derived product use or bleeding outcomes. Although fibrinogen concentrations were higher and activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio were shorter at the end of CPB in the Pre-FFP group, these differences largely resolved after CPB. papers.abstract: Tumor necrosis is associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) yet is generally viewed as a passive consequence of tumor growth rather than a therapeutic target. We demonstrate that necrosis correlates with metastatic disease in human CRC independently of tumor size. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of primary CRC and colorectal liver metastases revealed that peri-necrotic programs are associated with metastatic progression. Patients with CRC exhibited increased circulating neutrophils, including NET-primed and CD177-low neutrophils with reduced extravasation capacity. Consistent with these findings, intravascular NET aggregates localized adjacent to necrotic regions in human CRC specimens. In a mismatch repair-proficient mouse model of CRC, neutrophil infiltration and NET formation increased during tumor progression, whereas genetic and pharmacologic NET inhibition reduced tumor necrosis, decreased metastasis, and enhanced chemotherapy efficacy. Together, these findings identify NET-driven tumor necrosis as an active promoter of CRC metastasis and support NET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for multiple myeloma (MM), yet the burden attributable to high body mass index (BMI) in BRICS countries remains unclear. This study assessed temporal trends, regional variations, and future projections of this burden. Data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study were used to estimate the incidence, mortality, prevalence, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of MM attributable to high BMI during 1990-2023 across Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. Age-period-cohort modeling, joinpoint regression, decomposition analysis, and Bayesian age-period-cohort forecasting were applied to evaluate trends and project the burden through 2040. Globally, deaths and DALYs increased substantially during 1990-2023, while age-standardized rates increased more modestly. Considerable heterogeneity was observed across BRICS countries. India showed the most rapid long-term increase, China accounted for the largest absolute burden in 2023, and South Africa exhibited among the highest age-standardized rates, whereas the Russian Federation showed a recent declining trend. Decomposition analysis indicated that population growth was the predominant contributor to the global increase, while epidemiological change represented the major contributor in China and India. Age-period-cohort analysis demonstrated that the burden was concentrated among older populations, with increasing risks observed in more recent periods and birth cohorts, particularly in countries undergoing rapid epidemiological transitions. BAPC projections suggested continued increases in the global burden and in most BRICS countries through 2040, whereas declining trends were projected for the Russian Federation. Sex-specific analyses showed a consistently higher burden among men, although sex differences varied across regions. The high BMI-related MM burden in BRICS countries is rising, with distinct regional patterns driven by demographic expansion and changing risk profiles. Targeted obesity prevention, cancer surveillance, and equitable access to MM diagnosis and treatment may help mitigate the future MM burden.

papers.abstract: Retrospective studies and analyses of RCTs showed that surgical quality of mesorectal excision affects oncological outcomes of rectal cancer patients. Objective of this study was to determine the impact of mesorectal excision quality on local recurrence and overall survival in rectal cancer patients. MEDLINE was searched till April 1, 2024, with MeSH terms: rectal cancer/neoplasm, total mesorectal excision, TME, rectal cancer surgery, macroscopic assessment/evaluation, quality/adequacy/completeness of surgery/mesorectum/resection specimen, prognosis, and outcome for randomized clinical trials, prospective and retrospective cohort studies reporting oncological outcomes and quality of the mesorectal excision. The main outcome and measures were local recurrence and overall survival. TME quality was classified into three grading categories (complete or mesorectal resection (MRR); nearly complete or intramesorectal resection (IMR); incomplete or muscularis propria resection (MPR)). Of 438 records screened and an additional three studies by cross-referencing, 15 articles with 11,285 individual patients were identified. Median age of included patients was 63, 55 (range 21, 0-95, 0). Pooled incidence of good (MRR), intermediate (IMR), and insufficient (MPR) TME quality was 65, 6%, 22, 8%, and 11, 6%, respectively. Insufficient TME quality was associated with locally advanced tumors. No difference in TME quality was observed between patients with and without neoadjuvant therapy. Pooled analysis showed lower odds for LR and higher odds for OS in patients with good TME quality, which is also shown in a subgroup analysis of neoadjuvantly treated patients. In conclusion, this meta-analysis confirms that good TME quality is associated with lower risk for local recurrence and higher probability for overall survival, an association that persisted also in neoadjuvantly treated patients. These findings suggest that neoadjuvant therapy will not compensate for suboptimal surgical quality; however, given the substantial heterogeneity across the included studies and the limited availability of data on contemporary treatment regimens, they should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

papers.abstract: People with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; hereafter, PWH) face differences in cancer treatment and quality. In a cross-sectional survey (December 2022-August 2025) of 120 PWH diagnosed with cancer and receiving care at an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center in Florida, we examined associations of HIV stigma (Berger HIV Stigma Scale) and everyday discrimination (Everyday Discrimination Scale) with cancer care quality (Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems [CAHPS], Patient-Centered Communication in Cancer Care [PCCC], Health Care System Distrust, and Barriers to Care scales). Multivariable linear regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and cancer type. Personalized stigma was associated with lower PCCC fostering healthy relationships (β: -0.29; 95% CI: -0.56, -0.01). Disclosure concerns were associated with worse care coordination (β: -0.23; 95% CI: -0.46, -0.01), greater distrust (β: 0.23; 95% CI: 0.05, 0.41), and greater barriers to care (β: 0.19; 95% CI: 0.01, 0.38). Everyday discrimination was associated with lower global healthcare ratings (β: -0.41; 95% CI: -0.71, -0.11). This is the first quantitative evidence that HIV stigma, particularly disclosure-related facets, undermined measurable cancer care quality.

papers.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is an essential type of circular DNA that is mainly characterized by independence from chromosomes and a broad size distribution. Increasing evidence suggests that the distinctive genomic distribution of eccDNA establishes it as a clinical biomarker. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying its biogenesis and function in tumorigenesis have not been fully elucidated. Thus, in this review, we summarize the emerging insights into the biogenesis mechanisms of eccDNA, with particular emphasis on the recently described single-strand break driven internal loop (i-loop) model. We also discuss its critical roles in oncogenesis, including oncogene amplification, tumor heterogeneity, cell death, tumor immunity and drug resistance. We further outline current detection methods for eccDNA and evaluate its potential as a promising diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarker for human cancers, as well as a therapeutic vulnerability with implications for chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy and nanotherapy.

papers.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) analysis provides a minimally invasive approach to breast cancer assessment across early detection, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and treatment adaptation in advanced disease. This review evaluates these applications by distinguishing analytical validity, clinical detection performance, prognostic validity, and clinical utility. In early detection, assays integrating genomic, epigenomic, fragmentomic, and protein-based features have shown encouraging performance in evaluated cohorts; however, sensitivity remains limited in low-burden disease, particularly stage I breast cancer. Their potential clinical role depends on the incremental information they provide beyond established imaging and diagnostic pathways. In the curative-intent setting, circulating tumor DNA detection after treatment is associated with recurrence risk and can precede clinical or radiographic relapse, supporting prognostic stratification and the design of MRD-guided intervention trials. Whether such interventions improve clinical outcomes remains a central unresolved question. In advanced breast cancer, plasma genotyping supports treatment selection in defined molecular contexts. Randomized trials of ESR1 mutation-guided endocrine switching have demonstrated progression-free survival benefits with specific treatment strategies, providing evidence beyond biomarker-outcome associations, although overall survival benefit remains to be established. Across applications, interpretation depends on assay characteristics, molecular input, disease setting, sampling schedule, and the clinical decision being evaluated. Future studies should connect assay performance to patient benefit through comparison with existing care, clinically meaningful endpoints, and assessment of treatment burden and downstream investigations. This approach will help define where cfDNA testing can contribute meaningfully to breast cancer management.

papers.abstract: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing. Patients with IEC-EC had 100-fold more CAR T cell persistence in the peripheral blood than patients without IEC-EC. RNA sequencing analysis revealed increased cytotoxic and inflammatory programs associated with the CAR+ infiltrates relative to controls. Clonal vector integration occurred in introns of highly expressed genes without evidence of vector-mediated mutagenesis. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In sum, we find that IEC-EC pathology represents a distinct, duodenum-predominant, clonal lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the infiltration of clonal CAR+ cytotoxic T cells into the gastrointestinal tract.

papers.abstract: Metastases arise when cancer cells disseminate from the primary tumor, or other metastases, and seed tumors at distant anatomical sites. Reconstructing migration histories from DNA sequencing data is key to understanding the cellular mechanisms underlying metastatic dissemination. While the data often support many equally plausible histories, current methods return a single solution or sample alternatives without guarantees of optimality or completeness. Here we introduce MACH2, which enumerates all optimal migration histories and summarizes them to identify high-confidence migrations. MACH2 combines existing parsimony criteria with a new criterion that minimizes the number of clones assigned to locations where they were not observed, and includes MACH2-viz, an interactive tool for exploring solutions. Using simulated tumors with known ground truth, we show that MACH2 outperforms existing methods. Across 145 lung, ovarian, breast and prostate cancers, MACH2 reveals extensive uncertainty in migration histories, infers histories consistent with orthogonal experimental data, and finds metastasis-to-metastasis seeding and linear progression to be common.

papers.abstract: Long-term survival after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (dCCRT) remains limited in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We evaluated induction immunochemotherapy followed by dCCRT and consolidation immunotherapy in this setting. This prospective, single-arm Phase II study enrolled 54 adults selected for definitive nonsurgical treatment. The planned regimen comprised two cycles of induction immunochemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, and a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor, followed by dCCRT with 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and concurrent weekly chemotherapy. The same PD-1 inhibitor was planned as consolidation therapy for up to 1 year. The primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate. Fifty-three patients (98.1%) completed two induction cycles, all 54 proceeded to dCCRT, and 31 (57.4%) received consolidation immunotherapy. Among all 54 enrolled patients, the 2-year OS and progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 84.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 75.2%-95.0%) and 61.5% (95% CI, 49.5%-76.4%), respectively, after a median follow-up of 28.1 months. Adverse events occurred predominantly during dCCRT and were mainly hematologic; lymphopenia and esophagitis were among the most frequent toxicities. Exploratory analyses suggested that suboptimal response after induction immunochemotherapy was associated with shorter PFS. The survival outcomes observed with this sequential approach support further evaluation of its comparative clinical benefit in randomized studies. papers.abstract: Immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis (IEC-EC) is a delayed toxicity of ciltacabtagene autoleucel. The US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium retrospectively adjudicated 54 suspected cases from 8 institutions: 41 were IEC-EC (31 confirmed by anti-camelid variable heavy-chain immunohistochemistry, 10 probable). Through September 2025, cumulative incidence was 3.0% (39 of 1,308 ciltacabtagene autoleucel recipients; 95% CI 2.1-4.1%); 12-month competing-risk incidence was 3.0% (95% CI 2.1-4.1%). Median symptom onset was 75 days after infusion. Grade ≥3 diarrhea occurred in 85% (34 of 40 with diarrhea); 73% (30 of 41) required parenteral nutrition. Despite normal upper endoscopy in 41% (9 of 22), duodenal biopsies showed villous blunting, apoptotic bodies and a dense cytotoxic T cell infiltrate, CD4+ in 61% (19 of 31), CD8+ in 26% (8 of 31) and mixed in 13% (4 of 31). A dominant T cell clone was detected in 76% (13 of 17 tested). Delayed neurotoxicity co-occurred in 41% (17 of 41). At last follow-up, 32% (13 of 41) resolved, 27% (11 of 41) had ongoing symptoms and 41% (17 of 41) died with active IEC-EC. Combined biologic and T cell-directed therapy yielded the highest resolution (55%, 6 of 11) in small subgroups. IEC-EC is potentially fatal and requires systematic evaluation and early directed therapy.

papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is uniquely vulnerable during armed conflicts because it depends on immovable equipment, trained staff, daily patient travel, reliable infrastructure, and uninterrupted access to treatment records. We describe the experience of the Department of Radiation Oncology at the American University of Beirut during two episodes of intense conflict affecting Lebanon in 2024 and 2026. We specifically focus on the closure of a satellite clinic and how we managed the resumption of care for displaced patients. Based on this experience, we propose practical preparedness measures for radiotherapy services in conflict-prone regions, including live off-site patient registries, predefined transfer workflows, regional radiotherapy capacity mapping, triage concepts, financial agreements, national coordination, and a wartime escalation framework. Radiotherapy preparedness should be treated as a routine component of cancer care in unstable regions, not an emergency exercise begun only after treatment has already been interrupted.

papers.abstract: Social and emotional support (S&E support) is an underexamined determinant of cancer survivorship, and its interplay with food insecurity is poorly characterized. We sought to quantify inadequate S&E support and evaluate its independent and joint associations with food insecurity and health outcomes among cancer survivors. Using 2022-2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data, 13,104 respondents with a history of cancer and 26,208 matched non-cancer controls were identified. Survey-weighted logistic regression models assessed associations between inadequate S&E support, food insecurity, and health outcomes, adjusting for sociodemographic and behavioral factors. Among 39,312 respondents, mean age was 67.1 years (SD 11.5), 60.1% (n = 23,700) were female and 77.2% (n = 32,979) identified as non-Hispanic White. Approximately half had annual household income ≥ $50,000 (54.6%, n = 16,604), never smoked (54.0%, n = 20,662), and reported no alcohol use (54.7%, n = 19,489). Among cancer survivors, respondents who were never married (aOR 1.74, 95%CI 1.12-2.69) or divorced/separated (aOR 1.75, 95%CI 1.25-2.46) had greater odds of inadequate S&E support, whereas higher income was protective ($50,000-$99,999: aOR 0.61, 95%CI 0.44-0.83; ≥$100,000: aOR 0.35, 95%CI 0.23-0.53). Inadequate S&E support was associated with higher odds of food insecurity (aOR 2.58, 95%CI 1.77-3.74), poor general health (aOR 2.78, 95%CI 2.13-3.62), poor physical health (aOR 1.95, 95%CI 1.48-2.57) and poor mental health (aOR 3.76, 95%CI 2.83-5.01). In stratified analysis, inadequate S&E support was linked with higher predicted probability of poor general health among food-secure (47.0%, 95%CI 41.2-52.9 vs. 27.3%, 95%CI 25.2-29.4) and food-insecure (54.5%, 95%CI 42.9-66.0 vs. 42.6%, 95%CI 33.2-52.0) cancer survivors. Inadequate S&E support clustered among socioeconomically disadvantaged cancer survivors and was independently associated with adverse health outcomes. Joint exposure to inadequate S&E support and food insecurity identified the poorest health profiles, supporting integrated psychosocial and material support in survivorship care.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) commonly develops intrinsic or acquired resistance to gemcitabine (GEM), limiting clinical benefit. To uncover the underlying chromatin and transcriptional programs and identify actionable targets, we integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq in a GEM-resistant AsPC-1 subline (AsPC-1 GR) and parental cells. Although global chromatin accessibility decreased in AsPC-1 GR, a set of resistance-specific open regions (Peak_up) emerged. Integrating Peak_up with resistance-upregulated genes (DEG_up) identified 916 candidate resistance-associated genes, and motif analysis further narrowed the regulatory candidates to 23 core transcription factors, with EGR1 prioritized. EGR1 knockdown increased GEM sensitivity and reduced clonogenic growth, whereas EGR1 overexpression promoted survival and tumor growth and weakened GEM efficacy in xenografts. Mechanistically, EGR1 suppressed GEM-induced pyroptosis, with reduced LDH release and decreased IL-1β, consistent with inhibited caspase-1/GSDMD signaling. Multi-evidence integration identified 26 EGR1-linked resistance genes; TCGA survival analysis and validation highlighted SERPINB1 as a key downstream effector. SERPINB1 promoted GEM tolerance by restraining caspase-1 activation, GSDMD cleavage, and cytokine release, indicating inhibition of pyroptosis. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry revealed EGR1 interaction with WDR5, and WDR5/SET1A positively regulated SERPINB1. ChIP-seq data mining and ChIP-qPCR showed co-enrichment of EGR1, WDR5, SET1A, and H3K4me3 at the SERPINB1 promoter, supporting an EGR1-driven epigenetic activation model. Therapeutically, IT25, an inhibitor of EGR1 DNA-binding activity, downregulated SERPINB1, restored GEM-induced caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of GEM in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify the EGR1-WDR5/SET1A-H3K4me3-SERPINB1 axis as a key driver of GEM resistance in PC and suggest that IT25-based combination therapy may improve GEM efficacy by reactivating pyroptosis.

papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory central nervous system (CNS) disease. Although current immunotherapies control relapses, they have limited impact on progression, which might reflect incomplete access to or modulation of compartmentalized CNS inflammation. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells can infiltrate tissues, but their ability to access and eliminate immune cells residing in the CNS remains elusive. We report the treatment of five individuals with progressive or relapsing-remitting MS with autologous CD19 CAR T cells to assess safety-relevant aspects, CNS bioavailability, and compartment-specific effects. The intervention induces remodeling of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) B cell pool, with a sustained reduction in CSF humoral biomarkers. Notably, CSF-infiltrating CAR T cells selectively upregulate phosphodiesterase 7B, while reconstituted peripheral B cells show altered cytokine and homing profiles. These findings indicate compartment-specific immunomodulation beyond peripheral B cell depletion and support controlled trials to test safety, durability, and efficacy.

papers.abstract: To report mature safety, urinary outcomes, PSA response, and biochemical control after 24-Gy single-dose radiotherapy (SDRT) versus 45 Gy in 5 fractions in two independently randomized PROSINT cohorts of intermediate-risk prostate cancer. This pooled analysis included 59 evaluable patients randomized locally (45 Gy/5 fractions, n=30; 24-Gy SDRT, n=29). Treatment-related safety was primary, anchored to grade ≥3 genitourinary (GU) or gastrointestinal (GI) events within 3 months (NCI CTCAE v4.0). Acute and late toxicity were ≤90 and >90 days after treatment, respectively. IPSS was modeled longitudinally using generalized estimating equations; PSA kinetics descriptively and biochemical relapse-free survival (bRFS) by Kaplan-Meier/Cox methods. The analysis was not designed for equivalence or noninferiority; efficacy analyses were exploratory. Median follow-up was 60.2 months. No treatment-related grade ≥3 GU or GI toxicity occurred (0/59; 95% CI, 0%-6.1%). Acute grade 1 GU toxicity was 53.3% with 45 Gy/5 fractions and 75.9% with SDRT (P=.103), and GI toxicity 10.0% and 24.1%, respectively (P=.181); no acute grade 2 events occurred. Late GU grade 1 toxicity was 36.7% with 45 Gy/5 fractions and 62.1% with SDRT (HR, 2.04; 95% CI, 0.96-4.32), whereas grade 2 remained uncommon (3.3% vs 10.3%; HR, 3.19; 95% CI, 0.33-30.71). Late GI toxicity was rare. Overall treatment-related grade ≥2 GU/GI toxicity was 6.8%/3.4%. Despite more frequent clinician-reported low-grade GU events after SDRT, IPSS increased transiently at 1 month and recovered toward baseline by 3 months in both arms; the between-arm difference in 1-month change was 2.7 points (95% CI, -1.80 to 7.16), with no evidence of differing longitudinal patterns (P=.733). PSA suppression was deep and sustained, with median PSA of 0.30 ng/mL after 45 Gy/5 fractions and 0.36 ng/mL after SDRT at 36 months. Eleven biochemical failures occurred (5 after 45 Gy/5 fractions; 6 after SDRT); 60-month bRFS was 85.1% (95% CI, 65.1%-94.2%) versus 80.5% (95% CI, 59.2%-91.5%) (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.31-3.50). Clinically significant treatment-related toxicity was uncommon after both regimens. Low-grade GU events were more frequent after SDRT, while patient-reported urinary symptoms recovered toward baseline in both arms. PSA suppression was deep and sustained, but comparative disease-control estimates remained imprecise. These findings support continued prospective evaluation of 24-Gy SDRT with adequately powered disease-control endpoints.

papers.abstract: HEV infection is an underappreciated differential diagnosis in patients presenting with acute hepatitis during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. As T-cells are the key targets of ICIs, particularly through blockade of inhibitory immune checkpoints such as PD-1, this intervention is likely to influence the dynamics and differentiation fate of de novo primed virus-specific T-cells during primary HEV infection. We therefore aimed to examine how PD-1 blockade during primary HEV-infection influences expansion, contraction, and memory formation of virus-specific CD8+ T-cells. HEV-specific CD8 and CD4+ T-cells were analyzed by applying a reverse phenotyping approach combined with single-cell transcriptomics and TCR sequencing, as well as multiparameter flow cytometry with MHC class I tetramers. We characterized HEV-specific T-cell responses in patients receiving ICI and in untreated patients during acute-viremic infection and after viral clearance. Under ICI, de novo primed HEV-specific CD8+ T-cells showed enhanced clonal expansion, cytotoxicity, and terminal differentiation. Rather than transitioning into classical memory subsets, these cells retained a cytotoxic transcriptional program and acquired features of long-lived effector-like T-cells (LLEC). While HEV-specific T-cells remained detectable over > 2 years, their functional recall responsiveness declined in ICI-treated patients. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that PD-1 blockade during the formation of a primary immune response reshapes the fate of the antiviral CD8+ T-cell pool, favoring terminally differentiated effector states over conventional memory formation, with potential implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies. Our study represents the first demonstration in a human model that PD-1 blockade during primary antigen exposure reshapes antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector formation and memory differentiation. By identifying PD-1 signaling during a primary immune response as a regulator of antiviral CD8+ T-cell fate, our findings establish a conceptual framework for understanding how immune checkpoint blockade influences the development of primary antiviral T-cell responses, with implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Cisplatin resistance critically limits muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) therapy, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we report that NOP2, an RNA m5C methyltransferase, is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant bladder cancer cells and clinical tumor samples, correlating with poor chemotherapeutic response. Mechanistically, P300-catalyzed lactylation at NOP2 K772 disrupts its association with the E3 ligase PJA2, thereby evading K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Stabilized NOP2 deposits m5C modifications within the coding sequence of GLS1 mRNA, which are recognized by the reader YBX1 to enhance GLS1 transcript stability and translation. Elevated GLS1 reprograms glutamine metabolism, augments glutathione and NADPH pools, suppresses ferroptosis, and drives cisplatin resistance. Notably, genetic depletion of NOP2 or GLS1, or pharmacological targeting with the GLS1 inhibitor CB-839, restores cisplatin sensitivity and synergizes with the ferroptosis inducer RSL3 in vitro and in vivo. Our findings uncover a lactylation-dependent stabilization of NOP2 and define a NOP2-GLS1 epitranscriptomic-metabolic axis that links m5C remodeling to ferroptosis evasion in chemoresistant MIBC, suggesting that interrupting this cascade represents a viable therapeutic strategy to overcome cisplatin resistance.

papers.abstract: Interferon gamma (IFN-γ) is a pleiotropic cytokine with a central yet complex role in anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. However, the key cellular sources of IFN-γ that are required for therapeutic efficacy remain undefined. We generated novel genetic models enabling cell type-specific Ifng deletion to selectively ablate IFN-γ production in CD8+ T cells, CD4+ conventional T cells (Tconvs), regulatory T cells (Tregs), or natural killer (NK) cells. MC38 and YUMMER1.7 tumor growth, survival, and responder ratios were assessed following anti-PD-1 or IgG control treatment. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were immunophenotyped by flow cytometry for evaluation of effector T-cell, exhaustion and activation markers. Two-way analysis of variance with mixed-effects modeling was used to compare tumor growth curves, and log-rank (Mantel-Cox) tests were performed for survival analysis. For flow cytometry analysis, statistical comparisons used two-tailed Mann-Whitney tests (multiple comparisons, 5% false discovery rate). Fisher’s exact tests were used for responder-class distributions. We demonstrated that IFN-γ derived specifically from CD8+ T cells was required to drive anti-PD-1-mediated tumor control. This effect was not observed on deletion of Ifng in CD4+ Tconvs, Tregs, or NK cells. Additionally, IFN-γ from CD8+ T cells was critical to promote TCF1+ and CXCR3+ CD8+ T cells while restricting terminally exhausted-like T-cell subset driven by anti-PD-1 treatment. Cell-intrinsic IFN-γ responsiveness by CD8+ T cells, via IFN-γ receptor 1 (IFNγR1), was dispensable for therapeutic efficacy. Our findings highlight CD8+ T cells as the critical source of IFN-γ for anti-PD-1 efficacy, highlighting an obligate paracrine mechanism within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract: The 2025 UK Code of Practice revised adult death determination using neurological criteria, including requirements for temperature, apnoea testing, and other aspects of assessment. National audit data describe how often testing occurs and record reasons for non-testing, but do not establish the consistency, quality, or physiological consequences of individual assessments. Testing rates were declining before the revised Code, precluding simple attribution of that decline to its introduction. We propose prospective patient-level evaluation from a predefined clinical screening trigger through assessment to confirmation of death, identification of persisting brainstem function, circulatory death before completion or after withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment, or continued treatment. A proposed dataset combines assessment timelines, individual prerequisites, test results, successive barriers, physiological events, and clinician experience. These findings should distinguish inconsistent interpretation from difficulties arising despite correct implementation and identify priorities for clarification, training, or focused evidence review.

papers.abstract: General anaesthesia for Caesarean delivery is increasingly used as a quality indicator, but general anaesthesia rates alone are not measures of quality. The multinational anaesthesia practice for Caesarean delivery snapshot study demonstrates variation in general anaesthesia use across European centres, emphasising the need to interpret these rates within the systems in which anaesthetic decisions occur. We propose an interpretation framework based on three domains: access to appropriate neuraxial care, reliability of neuraxial techniques and rescue pathways, and patient experience. The rates of general anaesthesia for Caesarean delivery should prompt investigation of system capacity rather than serve as verdicts on quality or safety.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies, with its incidence and mortality rates remaining particularly discouraging. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving PDAC progression and identifying potential therapeutic targets are critical to improve the clinical prognosis of PDAC patients. Accumulating evidence has highlighted the pivotal functions of centromere proteins (CENPs) in tumor progression. Accordingly, this study aimed to screen and identify key CENP family members implicated in PDAC pathogenesis. Through systematic analysis of CENP family proteins in PDAC, we identified CENPT as a critical regulator involved in disease progression. We further validated that CENPT promoted the proliferation and metastasis of PDAC cells via activating the RAF/MEK/ERK signaling pathway through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments. In addition, CENPT was also found to be implicated in tumor microenvironment remodeling. Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses demonstrated that CENPT expression was positively correlated with Treg cell abundance and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Further experiments suggested that CENPT upregulated the synthesis and secretion of MIF in PDAC cells, which acted on naive CD4+ T cells to promote the differentiation into Treg cells. This process ultimately induced the formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and facilitated PDAC progression, whereas blockade of MIF enhanced the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade for PDAC. In conclusion, this study revealed the crucial role of CENPT in PDAC progression, and targeting CENPT may serve as one of the potential therapeutic strategies for PDAC.

Second, the therapeutic recommendation for hesperidin lacks any functional validation, as no enzymatic, cellular, or in vivo assays were performed. These concerns fundamentally affect the validity of the paper's therapeutic conclusions and warrant clarification.

papers.abstract: Genomic assays guide adjuvant treatment decisions in early-stage hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer, yet contemporary treatment patterns and outcomes among premenopausal women remain incompletely characterized, particularly as adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors enter routine use. We characterized adjuvant chemotherapy use and its association with overall survival (OS) in premenopausal women with early-stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer, stratified by Oncotype DX recurrence score (RS) and by eligibility for adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy. In this retrospective National Cancer Database (NCDB) analysis, we identified 19,419 premenopausal women (age < 50 years as a surrogate for menopausal status), diagnosed with stage I-III HR+/HER2-, clinically node-negative (including those pathologically node-positive) invasive breast cancer between 2018 and 2022. Primary and secondary exposures were adjuvant chemotherapy and CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility. The primary outcome was OS. Cox proportional hazards models with robust variance were adjusted a priori for age, RS, and positive lymph nodes, with additional RS-stratified analyses. Overall, 13,490 women (69.5%) received no adjuvant chemotherapy. Chemotherapy receipt rose with genomic risk and CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility, while OncotypeDX testing was least frequent in the highest-risk groups. Adjuvant chemotherapy was independently associated with improved OS overall (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.47-0.86). In RS-stratified analyses, the association was limited to RS 21-25 (aHR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.68) and unknown RS (aHR 0.61, 95% CI 0.42-0.89). Adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved OS, mostly among RS 21-25 and a higher-risk unknown-RS group. Frequent absence of genomic testing among CDK4/6 inhibitor-eligible women highlights an opportunity to better integrate genomic and clinical-anatomic risk in treatment selection.

papers.abstract: Liver resections involving the hepato-caval confluence and/or retrohepatic inferior vena cava (IVC) sometimes require standard total vascular exclusion (TVE) with hypothermic perfusion. Veno-venous bypass (VVB) supports hemodynamic stability during TVE, but conventional external VVB carries risks including bleeding, air embolism, hemodynamic instability, hypothermia, and cannulation-site complications. Internal bypass alternatives have been described in liver transplantation but not previously in liver resection. We describe a novel internal porto-cavo-caval VVB technique-cavo-caval shunt (CCS) combined with temporary portocaval shunt (PCS)-performed during liver resection under standard TVE with hypothermic perfusion. The IVC is fully mobilized and lengthened via diaphragmatic hiatus opening; a reinforced PTFE graft is anastomosed laterally to the supra- and infrahepatic IVC, with a temporary PCS graft connecting the caval and portal systems. In one case, a pre-fashioned Y-shaped graft was used to reduce the number of anastomoses. The technique was applied in three patients undergoing extended hepatectomy for cholangiocarcinoma (n = 2) and alveolar hydatid disease (n = 1). TVE durations ranged from 90 to 120 min. All three procedures were completed without hemodynamic instability or complications attributable to the cavo-caval shunt. Postoperative courses included manageable complications unrelated to the bypass technique. All patients survived to discharge and remain alive at last follow-up. Internal porto-cavo-caval VVB via CCS with temporary PCS is a feasible alternative to external bypass during complex liver resection requiring standard TVE, preserving hepatic protection and bloodless exposure while avoiding external cannulation-related morbidity and core hypothermia.

papers.abstract: Anatomical resection of posterosuperior liver segments remains technically demanding because of the deep operative field, proximity to major hepatic veins, and variable Glissonean pedicle anatomy. We describe a robotic strategy integrating preoperative three-dimensional (3D) planning, hepatic vein-guided navigation, and indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence guidance. Resection was performed using the da Vinci 5 platform with four arms. Preoperative 3D reconstruction were used to identify the target Glissonean pedicles, the dorsal branch of the segment 8 pedicle (G8d) and the segment 7 pedicle (G7) and to define their spatial relationships with the RHV and IRHV, respectively. The strategy comprised three sequential steps: (1) a cranial approach to the RHV with G8d dissection; (2) a dorsal approach to the IRHV with G7 dissection; and (3) ICG fluorescence demarcation of the ischemic boundary followed by fluorescence-guided parenchymal transection. A 39-year-old woman underwent resection of a posterosuperior liver mass. Operative time was 220 min, estimated blood loss was 50 mL, and no transfusion was required. Pathology confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma arising in a hepatocellular adenoma. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 6 without complications. Robotic anatomical resection of segment 7 and the segment 8 dorsal area was feasible and safely completed using this structured strategy. Integration of 3D planning, hepatic vein-guided navigation, and ICG fluorescence may improve anatomical precision and reduce inadvertent vascular injury or incomplete anatomical transection in complex posterosuperior resections.
